author: DaxtotheMax
content: You saw the poster I assume? Well you're right. This is like an animated webtoon in terms of style so it's different. That isn't to say that the quality is dipped or anything, in fact, it looks quite good and well shaded. The plot lets you jump right into it. It's a similar situation to Life is Strange but one person sees the future of the photograph and the other jumps into the photograph and becomes whoever took the photograph for twelve hours after it was taken (unless they decide to jump out sooner). This builds an interesting dynamic between the two main characters, Cheng ... and Lu, Cheng being the time travel one and Lu being the mastermind. They both sort of use this as a basis for investigating, you see, they're not out to CHANGE anything, they're just out to find information, trying to take the same footsteps that the previous person did. It's all by request, sort of like a time traveling private investigator. But imagine if you DID want to change something. Becoming someone entails that you feel their same feelings and can share their same dreams but the personality is the difference. Lu is the one that tells Cheng not to get too attached and just focus on the mission (because they have a telepathic link going on). If you change something, think about that domino effect and how that can drive someone mad if you act out of character. The point of getting this information is to bring it back to the present to use in the future. Proof to indite someone. I won't spoil the ending of episode 1 but it really sets up what this series is about. The title is quite fitting in that way too because I watched that first episode and thought it was alright but then I slept on it and it really clicked for me, it has so much that I could want from it. It adds stakes by making each picture only able to be used once so no do-overs. It has an overarching story as well as contained arcs. They find new ways to reinvent the game so that no two missions are alike, you don't get too comfortable with just one way. I really appreciate exploring those possibilities. Now the ending is a bit...mixed in my opinion. I like the "idea" of the ending, there's a lot there to like but some of it just kind of comes off as cheesy or a reach as to how it correlates to the situation. Cheng's speech in particular is very broad, some reasoning is flimsy, context as to how exactly Cheng found all those pictures at the end seems a bit shallower than it could be, it's like it's all begging to be expanded upon so they come back and are like "nah, we're doing a season 2, that's why it's flimsy." which I knew about beforehand but I just don't really like the way they did it. Still though, other than that, it's a great anime that I highly recommend for people who like time travel, mystery, and stuff.

author: Prof-Harambe
content: Shiguang Dailiren shows a level of maturity that isn't so common in Japanese media, with surprisingly realistic characters blended into a realistic world, with hits of fiction such as the supernatural element which lends itself to an interesting premise. Lots of typical Japanese anime stray away from a lot of the concepts in the show in pursuit of a more generic, easy to market product. Shiguang Dailiren has a post-graduate, young adult cast instead of the generic high school protagonists we are all used to. It is progressive, it uses its older audience to tackle more mature concepts like sex, relationships, alcohol, work, etc. The ... difference between this show is how it tackles mature concepts in a mature way, take the relationship of Xu Shanshan. Instead of a blushing, tsundere, tropey character, she is handle in a way which shows clear affection for her partner and instead of her partner being completely ignorant like a generic shounen protagonist, he realises her feelings but is conflicted in confessing them due to his complicated situation. It leads to a really interesting romance side story which is interesting because it's actually handled better than a lot of actual romance anime, despite this being a tiny side story. No offense to Komi-san fans, but it is a prime example of a poor romance. It is extremely stagnant, no sort of progression in the romance aspect across the series taking 302 chapters before even the premise of a basic relationship is established, when both characters are shown to have feelings for each other very early on in the series. Most characters in the series are very one-note, ticking off tropes such as the generic yandere character. Tadano is a one dimensional, self insert protagonist at his very worst. This sort of thing is too prevalent in Japanese media, which is why shows like NANA are very refreshing. Story 8: I rated the story an 8 because there is a lot we are missing so far, we have mainly explored the stories of the side characters, and while they are intriguing and well written each in their own right, we have a lack of characterisation for Lu Guang and Qiao Ling, not that they are badly written characters, its just their story is not explained yet. If it is handled in a way that is akin to how Cheng Xiaoshi's arc is handled, I can easily put this up to a 10. Art 10: I really like this art style, not only is the animation on point, the art direction is too. Each character has a lot of detail. Backgrounds are beautifully drawn too. One very underrated thing is how lighting is handled and the impact of it. For example, when Xu Shanshan walks into the back alley, you can see how amazingly the lighting is handled. It really makes it immersive, which is uncommon for a genre which usually takes away from immersion because of its animated style. It makes the show feel more mature, and adds to the excellent drama into the show. There is also art imagery, such as the juxtaposition between Cheng Xiaoshi's and Lu Guang's hair colour showing the differences in perspective between the two, with Lu Guang being orderly and law oriented, following the rules outlined and not wanting to change the past, while Cheng Xiaoshi is much more chaotic, wanting to change the past and giving into his emotions to try and prevent a future tragedy. Sound 10: OP and ED are great, doesn't have the typical Japanese 'engrish' which plagues a lot of Japanese media, both artists speak very fluently in their songs and also the lyrics make a lot of sense, both grammatically and in relation to the show itself. The background OST was very good at raising suspense, especially when it transitions into the ending after a suspenseful moment. The lack of sound should also be commented on, sometimes there is no song which is used for suspense or when characters are making an important statement. This is used to great effect. Character 10: Characters are this show's greatest feat. While we haven't got a lot of characterisation of Lu Guang and Qiao Ling, mainly due to the story revolving around Cheng Xiaoshi, this is not a reason to knock the show since its likely their stories will be covered in season 2. All the characters who were explored in the show were excellently done, Cheng Xiaoshi is a very sympathetic character, we can feel his struggles as we view the story mainly through his eyes, and the eyes of the characters he possesses. He not only feels his own emotions, but the emotions of the characters who he possesses. The show is great at making you feel like there is a genuine threat working behind the scenes. While the two protagonists possess the power to change the past, the villain behind the scenes is presented as a much greater threat, especially with the season cliffhanger. The protagonists are not overpowered, they actually do encounter some failures and the impact of these failures is profound on the emotional Cheng Xiaoshi. author: PlainCasual
content: Link Click has one of, if not the strongest pilot episodes I have ever seen period. Every single scene is there for a purpose, that furthers the plot or provides another insight into it’s world. I believe it is refreshing how seriously Link Click trusts not only it’s story but it’s viewers. It doesn’t have a lengthy exposition, some monologue about how the world and time travel system works, it gives the viewer bits and pieces and knows that the story of Link Click is engrossing enough that the viewer will be willing to stick around despite being confused. The characters feel human, the dialogue ... is cheeky and smooth especially if you understand Chinese, and I absolutely adore the way they portray each character. Even if there is a cliche, the cliche is executed well.  We see an overworked, hired just for looks female assistant that isn’t revolutionary, but what is, is the humanity painted into them. Through just the food they encounter’ the repulsing eggrolls that is the norm in her city life, the ones she view as comforting from her parents back home, it creates true moments where the viewer can empathize with the character on the screen. This is one of the most beautiful shows I’ve seen in a long while and I truly recommend anyone who is interested to give the first episode a try.

author: Mury0kush0
content: If you don’t have any experience with dongua (Chinese anime) then this is a good place to start. I’d recommend you to watch it in Chinese dub instead of Japanese dub and although the first few eps may sound a bit awkward and will make you want to switch to Japanese dub, you’ll get used to it I assure you. The opening (although it’s in English) and the ending (Chinese rap) go hardddd in the original omg, plus their original voice suits them more. Now about the series itself….it’s a great supernatural detective mystery thriller where one of the ml (white haired one, still can’t remember ... their names) has the ability to get into photographs to solve cases. Don’t expect any romance at all between anyone and I mean anyone in here….which is great I mean. (If you’re thinking it is shounen ai or yaoi it is NOT). The episodes and the events are connected throughout which is another plus point and keeps you hooked. The story is pretty good and makes you emotional at times. The only con I’d like to point out is don’t expect any backstory at all of anything…how they end up with superpowers, why they’re doing this job etc etc….there’s no explanation of anything whatsoever and you just need to accept various things along the way. This did put me off because as a long time anime watcher as I’m used to heavy back stories and good explanations and all. However, I still rated this so high is because of my overall experience. I mean if you keep the expectations away you’ll enjoy it a lot and that’s why I’m writing this here. Definitely a must try if you want to explore animes of other countries. I’m glad they’re catching up to the high standards finally as before I had a tough time getting into donghua’s… Also the season 1 ends in a cliffhanger and very bad cliffhanger so season 2 is going to be insane especially considering how long it is taking to come out. Really excited for next season <3 Btw the opening and endings go hardddd so don’t miss them!

author: Jamie_Banach
content: This show really surprised me as I continued to watch it. I wasn’t expecting much when I started it and did not know what it was about but I am so glad I gave it the chance. The plot is very good and so intriguing, definitely wanting to keep watching just to know what happens next and how it all works. Haven’t seen a show with a plot quite like this. The characters are just as intriguing as the plot, you don’t know much about them but as the show continues you want to know more. The characters can be relatable at times and the stories ... looped between the main story you can connect with are just as interesting as the main story. I would have given it a 10 but I hate cliffhangers. Very excited for season two though. I would recommend this show to anyone even a anime beginner.

author: Zapper7
content: Link Click is one of those rare anime that pulls you in from the very first episode and refuses to let go. Its unique concept of diving into photographs to relive and even change the past is so fresh, and it’s executed beautifully. The story hits that perfect balance between mind-bending twists and raw, emotional moments that leave you thinking long after the episode ends. The art style really deserves a shoutout—it’s vibrant, smooth, and captures the mood of every scene perfectly, whether it’s a lighthearted moment or something much darker. And let’s not forget the absolute banger intros that hype you up for every episode. But ... what really makes this anime shine is the brilliant duo of Lu Guang and Cheng Xiaoshi. Their friendship feels so real, with Lu Guang’s calm, logical nature balancing Cheng Xiaoshi’s impulsive but deeply empathetic personality. Their dynamic is the heart of the series and makes you root for them no matter how tense things get. If you’re looking for an anime that’s visually stunning, emotionally gripping, and full of surprises, Link Click is an absolute must-watch.

author: xanlyandriii
content: A show that transcends anime, a true magnum opus of the entire modern entertainment industry as a whole. The writers gave themselves such a powerful plot device with a cleverly designed take on time travel. Setting yourself up for success is all well and good, but you still need to drive it home. Fancying someone, the warm embrace of a loving parent, lust and greed. Resentment, misunderstandings, ego, desire, good intentions gone awry, loss and tragedy, acceptance and reconciliation. Children suffering at the hands of emotionally selfish and immature parents, yet still being held hostage to them through their own intrinsic need of being loved and validated ... by one's own parent. Guilt. Hope. That oh so familiar wish to change the past, that itchy inkling in the back of your head whispering "What if?". Feeling powerless. Questioning not just the meaning, but also the scale of one's own impact on the world, from tangible everyday actions to key decisions a person makes during their lifespan, all the way up to the overarching philosophical framework a person uses to navigate their life, from birth until death. Drawing a line between righteousness and rationality. Butterfly effect. Drive and ambition. Purpose. Intimacy. Self-actualization and self-realization. Regret. Jealousy. Trust and its abuse. The never ending dance between putting your own needs first and helping others or doing what is "right". Yearning for a catharsis. Relief. Free will. Balance. Fate. If you can think of an emotional or meta-philosophical topic, there is a good chance Link Click has impeccably encapsulated it in one form or another into a bite-sized piece of entertainment that will pierce right through you and even though it will hurt like a motherfucker, you can't help but beg for more. All of this wrapped in a clean, compelling, action-packed storyline with likeable characters that moves at just the right pace. Despite the episodes being 20~ minutes each (and that's including OP and ED), every episode is filled to the brim with substance, emotion, nuance and brain-candy for your mind to chew on - that is, if you're not too busy bawling your eyes out like I did. After nearly every episode, I had a very similar feeling to a one I would get after watching a top tier 90 minute anime movie, because every 20 minute bite of the show is so densely packed with multiple layers of content. I wanted to binge watch it, but several times I simply couldn't press play on the next episode since I wasn't done yet processing the one I just saw. Crisp art-style, likely the best OP in history and amazing soundtrack is just a bonus. If they somehow manage to improve on this in the upcoming second season, then top #5 database ranking is inevitable. The first season is sitting at #38 at the time of writing this review and frankly, it should be 20 spots higher. I imagine this is the type of show other writers look at and tears start rolling down their face as they open McDonald's website and navigate to the "Jobs & Careers near me" section. You need to watch this not now, but yesterday. Then watch it again.

author: ZeyderZawliet
content: SPOILER FREE REVIEW! English is not my native language, hope you oversee any mistakes, thank you! TL;DR in the 'overall section' "I've experienced many different lives, but there's always something I regret in almost every life" Link Click, a show having easily one of the best first episode I've ever seen even if you not into Time Travel genre, this show is extremely easy to get into, the rules of time traveling gets established in the few few minutes and they are simple enough to require no explanation. ... This show is seem completely episodic at first as the main plot only began surfacing in the latter half of the series, While the 'mini' stories are dedicated on personal, and the thriller aspect of the show, the main storyline focuses on the consequences of the MCs unintentionally messing with the past and also bringing mystery to the table. The show explores heavy concepts like the butterfly effect, predestination paradox in the main storyline(doesn't complicate the show and are subtle) and sticks to thrilling and emotional writing in the 'mini' stories, talking of them, they are the true highlights of this season, every story is a rollercoaster full of emotions, thrills and cliffhanging episode endings. Story: 8/10 The story writing is amazing on the sub-plots, all the characters featuring on them are very well developed considering their 1-2 episode(s) screen time. As I told before these are truly rollercoasters of emotions and thrills. (sub-rating 10/10) The 'main' plot however is lacking, kicks off pretty late in the story considering the 'main' plot and doesn't explain anything important like MCs' relationship with each other, their power origins, also little to no development on MCs except the protag(*more on the character section).  (sub-rating 4/10) Art: 9/10 I really love this webtoony artstyle, the backgrounds look amazing and shading is neat. No complains. Music/Sound: 10/10 The OP/ED are the best part of the show for me, Even when the show would end at the worst cliff hanger, my fingers refuse to skip the ED. Also the OSTs are great, adding even more dramacity(I just made that word up) to the dramatic scenes. Character: 5/10 Keeping aside the sub-plots' characters (As I told before they are great considering their screen time) From what I see, the only character that got any 'real' development is our protag- the blackhair guy and other dude feels like a new character in every episode for me(maybe his motives, backstory accidently got deleted from the script, who knows?) What? there was a supporting girl character in the series? pffffffffft the protag also gets a little,... little annoying after a while... won't say more, I maybe standing very close to the spoilers territory. Enjoyment: 9/10 I loved this show despite its lacking plot and character development, The 'mini' plots were amazing to me, felt like a cover up for their main plot but I think that's just because this season is dedicated to MC's exploring their powers, the next season will hopefully develop the main plot and bring massive development to the MCs also the cliffhangers on every single freaking episode will almost make anyone binge the entire series enjoyed a lot TL:DR/Overall: 9/10 [I highly prioritize 'enjoyment' in the overall rating] Definitely a show worth to try, the subplots are highlights of the show, the main plot and MCs are lackluster in development Artstyle is straight out of a web comic, I like it(subjective) OP/ED are AMAZING(subjective my ass) Try the first episode, that's basically how the entire series is. feeling really restraint making the review spoiler free, will prolly write an another review(with spoilers) of this series in the future HOPE YOU LIKED THE REVIEW, if not that's completely fine, check out the review below >_>

author: eqazec
content: I watched this series on the recommendation of a friend. I had never heard of it before he said this show was dope. Wow, does it ever impress! The premise is simple. One guy can see the past captured by a photo and the other guy can jump into the photo's past-timeline. They can't change the past in any significant way, but they can gather information to help the present. The whole series is a episodic mystery, involving an unusual form of time travel. It is amazing! *** I did my best not to include them, but there may be some spoilers *** The last two episodes ... were extremely impressive and logically sound. That last episode, though, was INSANE. In all my time watching the show, I had a million theories for how it would end, but I never would have anticipated exactly what came in the last 5 minutes of the show. I'm shocked by the events but equally curious to see how they are resolved in the next season. My only fear is that the writers will take the series in a direction that is out-of-place for the series, with its heavy emphasis on human nature as the driving force of plot action. I guess I'll find out if my high hopes are well-vested in a year or so. (EDIT: The studio says 1.5 years of production time starting from August 2021, but that they hope to reduce it.) Now, for a simple breakdown of the overall rating of 9: Music/Sound (9/10) - Extremely fitting and apt soundtrack for the series. The OP is a bop and the ED is perfectly timed to accentuate each episode's cliffhanger. Art (8/10) - The art, though simplistic at times, is a staple of Chinese Donghua. The rough aesthetic given off by every room/set-space is gritty and cements the series in the "dark and dreary world" where the MCs investigate heavy topics, like murder, fraud, rape, kidnapping, etc. Characters (8/10) - The characters are straightforward, but I give the writers an 8 for their excellent development of the side characters' and photo-peoples' personalities, despite their relatively brief appearances. I wish that Cheng XiaoShi was not the only MC whose background was deeply explored in this series. I would love to know where Lu Guang and Qiao Ling get their drives from. Even after the end of the season, I still struggle to understand exactly how/why Lu Guang and Cheng XiaoShi came to be friends, aside from their same abilities. Story (9/10) - The fresh and gripping storyline might compel one to binge watch the entire season in one sitting. The worlds of the photos are brutally realistic, and each new mystery solved feels like an opportunity to explore a new world from an entirely different anime. There are only a couple issues I had with the story's continuity in the last two episodes, but that mostly stems from the sudden introduction of the new plot mechanic. Enjoyment (10/10) - When it comes to mystery and drama series, I tend to be a very picky viewer. If the stakes are too high (i.e. MCs are nearly dying every episode), then I can't relax and watch it. The writers of《时光代理人》do a perfect job of "balancing the stakes." The MCs have two goals, gather information to change the present and don't change the past. The stakes are the possible irreparable damage to the timeline. I can sit back all day without having to worry that my main characters are going to die every two minutes. I could watch Cheng XiaoShi and Lu Guang run through photos all day, because the stakes aren't physically deadly, but are rather a metaphorical weight on the shoulders of the MCs. Overall (9/10) - GREAT! This series is simply great. The mysterious drama is easy to watch and enjoy while providing enough intellectual stimulation to not feel like a Shonen anime. The detective work they do is wild, but the characters are generally very realistic. With a guaranteed second season coming up, I believe Link Click has the potential to put Chinese DongHua even further into the spotlight with other mainstream animations.

author: PinkHairedPunk
content: I was instantly drawn to this anime because of the artstyle and I didn't even know what the story was about. With that said, I think this was a great way to get into the series as I explored the plot together with the characters instead of knowing more than them. This is my first ever review on here, because I just have to talk about this to someone (& my IRL friends won't listen xD) So: The first thing you'll notice is the art of course. It's so well done in my opinion. The colours and the lighting in each scene is done so carefully! ... It supports the whole atmosphere of the plot in my opinion - it's relaxing but at certain moments it gets thrilling. The second thing that got me hooked right from the start was the Sound! The OP is so good and the ED really adds to the mysterious aspects that happen at the end of almost each episode! I can listen to the OP & especially the ED forever and wouldn't even think of skipping them! (I even made the ED my screensaver on my laptop because of how nice the animation is there too!) The one thing that made me stay was the story and how the characters interact with eachother. author: Spenz7
content: As an avid manga reader, I always thought that given how bad manhua was, I believed that the same could be applied to animation. Oh boy was I wrong. Story: Whenever time travel is invovled, it can either go well or horribly wrong. Unfortunately, most of the time it is the latter instead. This is what sets the show apart from the rest in how it deals with time travel well by making it easy to understand and logical. Also, the show includes many life lessons that I find are applicable to many of us in real life. So its a definite yes when it comes ... to learning something good from this donghua. Art: Pleasing art style, not over and top and kept nice and simple. Sound: OP and ED are absolute bangers Character: 2 main characters that fit each other like ying and yang. Both complement each other's strengths and weaknesses well and the character development is easily a solid 8/10. Enjoyment: 10/10 as it gave me a whole new outlook on donghua and enjoyed how they didn't introduce too many characters and decided to focus on developing a select few instead which made it all to more of a rollercoaster ride as one is able to resonate with characters a whole lot better. Overall: Solid 8 but I'm going to give it 9 given how I couldn't find any significant flaws in the show but if i really had to nitpick, it would be that how they include a backstory so it took a couple of episodes to really get what exactly was going on. (probably just me given how clueless I am lol) Tldr: A must watch if you want to see some drama(the good kind where there actually isn't pointless screaming and actual life lessons to be learnt instead)

author: Wystaria
content: Story: 10     Art: 10     Sound: 10     Character: 10     Enjoyment: 10     Overall: 10 I don't typically feel compelled to leave reviews for highly-rated shows, but this donghua blew every other animated series I've ever seen completely out of the water. It is ABSOLUTELY incredible, and it's soul-crushing to see almost no one talking about it on the internet. So, without further ado, let's get into the review! This might be a bit long, so please bear with me. A short summary first: Guang Lu and Xiaoshi Cheng run ... a photo development studio. Though that may seem like a very ordinary and maybe even boring job, the two actually share the ability to dive back into time via photos. Together, they complete odd time travel-related jobs that are brought to them by locals while staying true to three rules: 1. Xiaoshi and Guang can dive into each photo for a maximum of 12 hours. 2. Xiaoshi must follow Guang's every direction. 3. "Past or future... just let them be." Now that I have the summary out of the way, I'll get into what I loved about this show. What drew me in from the get-go was the art. Man, is it stunning. When I first laid my eyes on the promotional poster, I thought, "This looks so different from any other animated series I've watched thus far... no way such quality is maintained through the show." I was both right and wrong! I guessed correctly that the series is not Japanese (it is, in fact Chinese, and hence a donghua, not an anime), but the consistency of animation quality is where my hypothesis missed its mark. The animation style is true to the art style of the poster, and I was hypnotized by it immediately. It's beautifully executed and a pleasure to watch in action. Not to mention that the opening theme and animation sequence immediately flexes on the viewers with complex animation of hand movements... it's a feast for the eyes. And speaking of the opening, the opening and ending themes are absolutely a pleasure to listen to. They starkly contrast and yet complement each other, and even though the subject explored by the opening theme is a bit on-the-nose, it's catchy and fun to listen to. Now, the characters! I CANNOT emphasize enough how much I love the characters in this donghua. I'm heavily biased towards Xiaoshi, but even the supporting characters are very likeable (with the exception of a few that I won't be mentioning for plot reasons) and well-written (yes, even the unlikeable ones). Guang and Xiaoshi make for a wonderfully dynamic duo; they work well together and complement each other's strengths and weaknesses very nicely, and as a whole, their friendship is natural and interesting to watch. Despite being nothing but arrangements of pixels with a connected identity moving across the screen, all of the characters feel like they could exist in real life. They're just... human. Also, did I mention how nice it is to see two people working together with time travel? I feel like it's tempting to make just one insanely capable main character when it comes to the topic of changing the future and past, but the fact that "Link Click" instead has two people guiding each other and working together is something that I really appreciate. When dealing with something as complex as time and butterfly effects, I find it difficult to believe that just one person would be capable of handling it. But I digress! The humanness is what I love about "Link Click" so much. Despite being primarily a drama and supernatural series, it tackles a variety of other genres: slice of life, romance, thriller... even sports! At its core, it is a series that discusses life as a whole and the human drama that, for us people, is its foundation. Every story in every episode feels real and emotional, and it hit me hard time and time again. I don't think I watched a single episode without shedding at least some tears. What's even more impressive to me is the plot consistency, and again, human perspective in relation to time. For me, "Link Click" 's nuance comes from its approach to the concept of alternate realities. It is within human nature to be skeptical, especially when it comes to time travel. "Just one tiny change wouldn't hurt anyone, right?" That is a question that Xiaoshi struggles with throughout the series, and it's a question that many of us have probably asked ourselves in relation to time travel. It's an honest, human question that I cannot fault Xiaoshi for exploring. When you're shoved into someone else's body and forced to confront their daily struggles and choices, it can be hard to resist the temptation to make just one tiny change for the sake of a better future. Literally anyone put in the same situation would probably make the same mistake. And yet, at the same time... sometimes, small changes can also lead to a happier present and future. author: Rwurg
content: You aren't ready for the ending... It seems rather innocent in the beginning.  But don't give up. If you are confused about what's going on, and how this universe works, that's intentional. It works you into the story. Starts you off slowly, and introduces different concepts and characters that you should pay attention to. I will admit, it may be difficult to see where the story is going at times. The two protagonists are great complements of each other, and offer comedic relief at times when necessary. They do very much drive the story forward, and you will feel yourself becoming connected to them. ... The art style is unique and refreshing. I like that it's something different, while at the same time, managing animations almost flawlessly. It's not at the same level as AOT or DS, but it does things better than most. One last thing I will say, I loved the concept of this story.  It's difficult to talk about this too much without giving away the story. If you enjoy mysteries and time travel, you will love this. This for me was a true masterpiece, no question. It kept me and my wife on the edge of our seats, so much so, where we were staying up late (with an infant child) to continue watching. (just wanted to edit to say that the ending song was an absolute banger, and fit perfectly ever time).

author: Makimasd0gg0
content: 𝐒𝐡𝐨𝐫𝐭 + 𝐒𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐒𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐫 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐢𝐞𝐰 : Link Click also known as Shiguang Dailiren is an original Donghua series produced by Haoliners Animation League.  As my first Donghua holy shit it's way better than I expected . The original story line and concept really  got me hooked into the show . The art style is really unique and different from what you regularly watch . The animation is pretty high quality as well . Opening , Ending and all the ost's are S tier. The reveal of each and different mysteries are perfectly balanced and really had me shook . You can't really predict ... what's going to come next . Each arc's are different and unique in its own way . Especially the earthquake one . That gotta be my personal fav . Through the whole series I felt different emotions in a good way ofc . Sometimes the reveal of mystery leave me shook , sometimes the emotions between two characters such as episode 5 really make me makes me emotional. The characters are really good and well well written as well. Cheng Xiaoshi is the black haired guy is somewhat you would call the "realist one" .He enters inside certain photos through someone else's body and does whatever Guang tells him too . Physically strong but mentally kinda weak and emotional makes him a well written character in my opinion . He is rather childish and stubborn who sometimes messes up with his own work and later regrets . Personally I can relate to him a lot . Lu Guang is Xiaoshi's friend or work partner whatever you prefer is rather the opposite of Xiaoshi . He is calm , rational and does his job perfectly without trying to mess with the time too much . He can look inside certain photos and also tells Xiaoshi to what to do so everything can be perfectly balanced . Sometime can be a little cold hearted due to not wanting to mess with the past too much , but it's actually for the better , As it reveals in episode 1 . And their designs are cool as well . Even the side characters are well written and depending on thier roll they are either likable or unlikeable . The art style is different from your average ones since it's not from Japan but that doesn't mean it's not good . The ost's are all Top tier . The soundtrack is really well and goes with the situations perfectly. The ending and opening songs are really good . I'm literally vibing whenever it plays and the hand and body movements are just chefs kiss . The storyline is 10/10 , the mystery , supernatural , drama are all well made and perfectly balanced as well . Overall , I really love this series cuz of it's unique storyline and dynamic . Being my first Donghua it really surprised me it . I honestly binged it all in one day which I usually don't normally . But everything about this series has really made me love it a lot . I would recommend anyone to watch this . At first it was a little hard to read the subtitles and I really had my own doubts weather it is actually good or not but as time passed i found out it's actually a top tier series and got used to the subtitles aswell . Overall I would say everything equal ( ost + characters + thier designs + soundtrack + storyline + animation + art style ) this series is 10/10 and I hope it gains more fans honestly .

author: RemanTheArchean
content: This review covers the first 2 seasons, as well as the "Bridon Arc". The show is composed of roughly two parts: the mystery-thriller that's mostly centered around the time travel mechanic, and the melodrama that's more interested in side stories of various characters. At first, the latter element gets much more screentime, with the time travel being little more than a means to go from one story to the next. The first half-dozen episodes almost take on this "melodrama of the week" quality, which, uh, if you've read my Violet Evergarden review (https://myanimelist.net/reviews.php?id=574604) you'd know I'm not a big fan of. I think episodic melodrama ... is particularly hard to do well, and while the scenarios here aren't quite as unbelievable as they were in Violet Evergarden, I still didn't find them particularly engaging, although I admit this might just be a "personal preferences" thing. On the other hand is the mystery-thriller time travel stuff, which gets more attention as the series progresses. It does this part quite well, at least for the first two seasons. The black-haired protagonist named Cheng Xiaoshi gets 12 hours to enter a person's body and pry useful information. There's also the white-haired protagonist named Lu Guang can see the future and guide him in keeping the past how it's supposed to play out. It's a mix of the Butterfly Effect where altering events can have unexpected (generally negative) consequences, with bits of Steins;gate in how only "critical moments" really matter. It's an interesting enough gimmick to carry a story, and the show really comes alive when the mechanics are a focus or when they're used in creative ways. The show is also helped by the characters mostly acting like adults -- a relatively rare thing in anime. I have some minor quibbles with how Cheng keeps getting emotional and comes very close to changing the past in ways the could ripple out to being Bad, but he doesn't actually go through with them for the most part. At the start of season 1, the show is roughly 70% melodrama and 30% mystery, while by the end of season 1 those ratios are flipped to 30% melodrama and 70% mystery. It continues with that pace into season 2, which is when the show is firing on all cylinders. It becomes almost a cat-and-mouse like Death Note, and I was hooked. A typical setup at that point is to show a scene without context, and have stuff that seems crazy or unbelievable happen, then it goes back and explains how everything worked. It's a good formula that maintains suspense and quickly answers the questions it brings up. None of the reveals feel like BS as they're typically only moderate extensions of the knowledge we already have of how the powers work, peoples' motivations, etc. while also doing more than enough to keep me guessing. That said, the melodrama also takes a turn for the worse here. Season 1's melodrama is fairly varied, but I hope you're fine with abused women being utilized as a plot device from S2 onwards, because this show REALLY likes to do that over and over. You'll see women beaten, abused, strangled, nearly raped, screamed at, and even murdered. It almost became a running gag, with whenever I saw a new female character introduced I would think to myself "I wonder when she'll get treated like a pinata", and I'd end up being correct most of the time. While S1's melodrama was merely "boring", S2's became outright repulsive, which was only helped somewhat by it having a lower screentime priority. Overall though, Season 2 is a decent package. The same cannot be said of the Bridon Arc, which MAL lists as a "side story", but it's 8 episodes (6 episodes really, but the first episode is a 3-in-1) worth of fairly critical information, so I doubt you'll be able to skip it. I don't know if some amateurs took over or what, but the show basically forgets how to do a mystery-thriller. The way it's supposed to go is question → partial answer → bigger question → partial answer. But here, all we get is question → question → question → question... Minor spoilers here, but to demonstrate what I mean I think an example would be helpful: in S3E1 a redhead character is revealed to be a bad guy since he attacks Lu Guang for reasons that aren't explained, then Lu Guang goes back in time to stop something that isn't explained, and he encounters the redhead who's all too eager to help the protagonists for reasons that aren't explained, then in E6 the readhead turns on them for reasons that aren't explained, using a nonlethal takedown on Cheng for reasons that aren't explained, then demands a macguffin (the purpose of which is not exlained), but then he also has a heart attack in the middle of the fight that instakills him for reasons that aren't explained, and then it's revealed he actually survived for reasons that aren't explained. You may have noticed I used the phrase "for reasons that aren't explained" over half a dozen times, and yeah, the whole season is 8 episodes worth of setup

author: xylidine
content: This anime genuinely blew away all expectations and is one of, if not, the best Chinese anime out there. The unique concept of the show creates interesting storylines and plots that are a breath of fresh air from every other other. A cliche in time travel shows is "don't change the past as it will cause devastating consequences in the future" is also in this anime, however the characters' actions make it very clear you literally CAN'T change the past and important nodes in time are always reached no matter what you try to do to prevent it. I went into this thinking it was ... going to be a typical time travel show, but was not ready for how emotional each episode was. Each client whose past was entered, brought with them a backstory that gave me chills and made me actually care about why they wanted to 'change' the past. There are also many cliffhangers in the show which were perfect and introduced a little bit of extra information, base upon what had happened in the episode. These twists that are implemented at the end of each episode will make your heart skip a beat and want to know where the story is going next. Trust me, you won't ever be able to predict what is coming. Overall, Link Click is a great anime which will keep you hooked with its unique time travel mechanics, emotional story telling and characters. 9/10

author: Aisukurimu
content: Hi pals of MAL, it’s me again! Back at it with another Chinese anime review. Shiguang Dailiren, where do I begin. It’s very, very impressive for an anime(donghua) original, it’s not based on a big IP, none of that manga spoilers or the manga was better. The cliff-hangers week after week is truly compelling. Heck even EP11 left us on the cliff, or shall I say it pushed me off the cliff. Time travel is no new subject, as the Chinese saying goes, it’s not embarrassing to have the same theme, it’s embarrassing for the one who did it worst. At a first glance, the ... first few episodes had little explaining and it’s difficult to see how anything ties in together, I supposed we are on the same boat as Cheng Xiaoshi who fail to see the consequences and the cases are just one-off requests. Later when everything unfolds, the closed loops make sense, and you just go HOLY SMOKES. I totally had that /oh/ moment when the time travel pieced together. Story: Entering the past through a picture taken at that point is definitely a fresh idea I have not personally seen before. However, the bigger highlight is its ability to resonate with all audience. The stories have covered love/platonic/family relationships, from real life natural disasters to real crime cases. This is well received with the Chinese audience with a rating of 8.3 on Douban (Chinese rating platform). The 2008 Sichuan earthquake was one of the most devastating natural disasters that took lives of thousands, while an international audience may not have as strong as attachment towards Xiaoshi’s actions, many Chinese people were sympathetic towards Xiaoshi’s actions to save our loved ones. The kidnapper was based on a real kidnapper who to this day still out there which the police haven’t managed to locate, sadly reality did not bring a happy end like the episode. As age get to me, I begin to feel these types of stories closer to the heart. The helplessness at work, distancing from friends once very close, parents growing old etc…each episode managed to pull a string in my heart. The time travelling aspect I will not try to explain because it will spoil the story, that’s the best bit. I will briefly mention Xiaoshi’s “hot-headed” actions, it may seem annoying to the audience, but we got to remember we are viewing this from an outsider god point of view, we know a lot of things the characters don’t know, Xiaoshi trying to change the past and save people is not crazy, it shows he’s a very caring empathetic character. And throughout the series, he learns the consequences of changing the past too. Hashtag character development. Characters: People might accuse Lu Guang and Cheng Xiaoshi to be queer baiting, which I digress. Think some people have gone a little crazy just watching two guys on screen together, and to be fair, it could be canon for all we know. The girlfriends in ep2 were named after staff working on the animation, the director revealed they have a CP name too. His explanation was “it’s difficult to come up with names, but when I thought about the characters I immediately thought of them(the staff, apparently they were really friends at uni, both dudes btw) so I insert them in.” Anyhow, at first glance, it seems Xiaoshi is the more interesting character, but I do think Guangguang has a lot of potential. Guangguang’s past is yet to be revealed, the official posters say his age is unknown which lead to a lot of speculation. Perhaps this will be revealed in season two. Art: If one ever read Korean Manhwa, the art style of Link Click might remind you of that. Yup, they commissioned the Korean artists @inplick for character designs. They got some big names working on this, they got a good connection with CoMix Wave, so a lot of staff from CW worked on this. Tanji Takumi as art director, known for working with Shinkai on 5cm, Your Name etc... Background art by Asami Tomoya, worked on Weathering with You, Fate Zero etc.. There are no major issues with the art, colourful, flows well, does the job. Sound: Best OP and ED this season, this slaps so hard!!!! The English lyrics are funky and catchy, you should really stop thinking about it…stop thinking about it, stop… I CAN’T. The lyrics are intricately written to match the story. Same with the insert songs, the lyrics and melody hit me hard and brings the right mood to the stories. Voice acting. I know the Mandarin is a pain for people, I even read comments that said Mandarin sounds ugly, fuck you and your Japanese superiority complex. The voice acting is actually not bad here, the dialogues are not stiff, it’s not the Japanese translated to Chinese kind of speech, it’s fully how Chinese people speak. Voice director A’Jie is also a very experienced famous Chinese voice actor/director. Overall great Donghua, might even be one of the best ones this year. Very looking forward to season two, hope the quality don’t drop (eyeing Li Haoling because he directed Flavours of Youth and we know how badly that went). Until ne

author: Khashishi
content: This is one of the best works of 2021, and perhaps one of the best of all time. It's a supernatural thriller with a hefty amount of mystery, suspense, action, and psychological trauma. There's a hint of strategy mastermind, and some mind fuck. Nearly every episode ends in a cliffhanger. The animation is fluid and expressive, with lots of scenes and character movement. You can see emotions in the character faces. And wow, get mesmerized by that choreographed animation in the OP. They sure aren't afraid of animating hands. The OP and ED both have amazing music. The ED music likes to kick in right as you ... hit a cliffhanger, and provides just the right kind of energy to make your jaw drop in excitement. (I recommend listening to the original ED and not the Japanese dub, which lacks the power.) There are also some beautifully voiced background songs which really hit the feels during certain moments. There's also a tension song which is good but starts to sound a little repetitive as it is used often. The work prioritizes story, keeping it moving at a fast pace, so there isn't time for a lot of character moments. We can gather a lot about Cheng Xiaoshi's values from his behavior and emotions during missions. Lu Guang is tougher to read. We can see his concern for Xiaoshi and protectiveness. But he seems to be keeping secrets and it's hard to get into his head, since he doesn't express as much as Xiaoshi. The side characters get decent development during the arcs which feature them, but Qiao Ling doesn't get much at all. With time travel, you might expect there to be some plot holes. But from what I can tell, the story is rock solid. It's not entirely clear which theory of time travel is being portrayed; that's part of the mystery. The story is just ripe for theory crafting. Perhaps some of this will get settled in the next season. We can see special care in which details are presented to the audience at what time, which leaves me hopeful that everything will be wrapped up cleanly by the end. If they keep at it, this might rival Steins;gate. The first two episodes give the impression that this is a strongly episodic work, with the second episode being mainly self-contained. But then we start to get story arcs that last several episodes, and we keep getting hints that what started in the first episode is not over. There is also episode 5.5, which is self-contained, but should be watched. The last few episodes start to tie things together. It seems like we are making progress, but we end up uncovering more mysteries. The cliffhangers keep you at the edge of your seat, but at the same time, they feel a little manipulative. I think it's fine, but it might leave you a bit angry. This is not BL: there's no evidence of romance between the MCs. However, episode 2 has two guest characters who appear to be in a lesbian relationship, if you care about that sort of thing.

author: YUKIE_OREKI
content: My general impression about this work: it is a highly formulated 'full score' essay. Let me brainstorm how creators came up with Shiguang Dailiren. Firstly, lets create a very fancy concept/ mechanism, travelling through time seems to be a good one! To differentiate from other time travelling anime, let's say they travel through photos. Next, lets create the main characters. Seems like there's lots of market potential for BL, lets create the main protagonists as black hair guy and white hair guy and let's make their interaction cute (gay). Next, lets make the audience cry and create some depth by referring to dark social issues ... (e.g. overworking, lost of ties with parents, children trafficker, the earthquake), what about just do them ONE BY ONE as side plot and the audience will for sure cry! Finally, we need a main plot. Let's make the villain someone who also has the power to travel through time! yay, we have created Shiguang Dairiren. Now, don't get me wrong, I am not saying a highly 'formulated' work is not good thing if it's done properly. In fact, I was moved by the episodes on the earthquake. Even though I can feel that the scriptwriter is trying to make me cry, I can't help but sympathise with the characters and soak up the newly bought tissue paper with my tears. However, the 'full score essay formula' only worked well in the beginning. Once it turns to the main plot, the show becomes confusing and ends very abruptly without leaving the audience a satisfying explanation. It seems that the villain is trying to 'find friends' by killing innocent people, which makes me ???? Lots of things are not explained well in the work, for example, there's a temporal paradox as everything is a 'close loop' as oppose to the parallel universe setting in 'stein's gate', why the main protagonists has the ability to travel through time, and also the motive of the antagonist. That is just to list a few. It seems to me that a lot of the things Shiguang Dailiren mentioned are just 'floating on the surface' without a solid base. And that's why I cannot rate the show highly. However, I did have a very fun time watching the show and I absolutely love the OP and ED!

author: Steblob

author: ResiWeebVersion
content: First, I have 12 hours to write this. Second, I must follow the guidelines. And third, I cannot change the past. Ok my analogy breaks down, but you guys get it... These are the rules for time traveling imposed by Lu Guang on his partner, Cheng Xiaoshi. Cheng enters a person inside a photo and does stuff in the past. It's not a particularly new premise, in fact, the show isn't too different from many others in it's category when it comes to turning back the clock. If you have seen a plethora of time-travel shows and are interested in the sci-fi aspect, you will not ... be impressed. However, Shiguang Dailiren is great in many different ways, and highly enjoyable to watch. I'll be giving a structured review with some delirious rambling at the end. --- Plot --- The story is structured so that it mainly focuses on subplots in the beginning, then slowly converges into the main plotline, namely catching a murderer. If that makes you think the beginning is boring, then you are gravely mistaken. The subplots are every bit as interesting as the main one, if not more so, because the show excels at establishing characters efficiently and immediately getting you emotionally invested. Aside from that, these stories are essential to setting the stakes and even turn out to be relevant to the murders. They also made me shed a tear or two, but I do try to keep emotions outside the plot section, like a professional. Ahem... the pacing. Some people find it a little meandering and inconsistent, which I can't entirely disagree with, however: I like it. I really do. It's fast, but definitely not too fast. It doesn't detract from the insane tension that's present in every episode, and the show balances emotional scenes with more action-y and move-plot-along-y scenes marvellously. In conclusion, the plot is solid and reeeelatively novel, but it's not the show's biggest strength. --- Characters --- So this is kinda a mixed bag. We have Lu Guang, the solemn sigma male guide. We have his boisterous partner, the grab-the-bull-by-the-horns Cheng Xiaoshi. And then we have responsible Qiao Ling, their manager/childhood friend, and then we have my criticism. The female characters are a bit weak. Not physically, probably (this show has taught me that rural chinese parents make their children eat a lot) but concerning the development of the story. All of their contributions to the plot are entirely overshadowed by those of their male counterparts. Their characterization is also sparser, which is forgiveable however, as the show takes a lot of time to develop and paint all its main characters. That doesn't mean the female characters themselves are bad in any way - they're awesome, actually, and have a LOT of potential. This is definitely not one of your run-of-the-mill mysoginistic anime, but that potential needs to be actualized. I'm expecting more in future seasons, especially from Qiao Ling. Now that we have the negative out of the way, we can move on to the shining beacon that is Cheng Xiaoshi, who the majority of the show's character work is focused on. Cheng is a fantastic protagonist. He's funny, playful, emotional, brave, and displays some admirable civil courage. He stays consistent, but he's not a stereotype, either. Throughout the story, Cheng progresses as a person, learning from his experience but staying relatable all the while. Chef's kiss on that one :<(-_-) All in all, the show gets you quickly and strongly invested in its characters, who are distinct, lively and realistic. --- Art and Music and Whatnot --- AMAZING. The artstyle is beautiful. As a non-Chinese person, the voice acting sounds pretty good to me. The animation ranges from (thankfully rare) awkward, janky movements to cream of the crop, fluid manipulation of space. Cursory scenes are kept low-budget, but the sequences that really matter receive all the technical love they deserve. There's a basketball game in episode two that I rewound twice, because it looked so stunning. I have no qualms. The music is another HUGE plus. There's some great emotional piano with strings, for which I immediately sat down at my E-board after finishing the show to transcribe. And of course the ending, which FRI. KING. SLAPS! How is it possible for me to dislike western rap but love Chinese one?? --- Incoherent, Uncontrolled Rambling --- Whew, finally we have reached the most anticipated section. First, I want to highlight something I really liked in Shiguang Dailiren. Since the dawn of my show-watching career, I have been giving the same advice to time travel shows that focus mostly on drama: Stop overexplaining. Stop it. Pls pls pls stop. But they never listen, no matter how much I imagine them listening. They always get tangled in a spaghetti mess of timelines seasoned with cans and cans of plotholes, because they focus really hard on rules that end up broken, and because they try to insert some bullshit pseudo-scientific explanation for how everything works. author: TsukiEmblem
content: If you are hesitant to watch this because it's Chinese and you're more used to Japanese, please do not let such a think deprive you of watching this hidden gem. This is easily one of the best animated shows I've ever seen and would easily stand against some of the best Japanese anime. If you liked shows like Steins Gate or Death Parade, I would highly recommend this as something similar. The way it handles time travel is refreshing and entertaining, and its commentary on life and relationships creates beautiful stories in each episode. The art is breathtaking, I found myself frequently admiring the animation ... and the official art is fantastic too. The opening and ending songs are unbelievably good, I listen to them on every car ride. They match with the show perfectly and I love the opening's visuals as well. Characters get some of the most unique development due to the story's time travel elements. As far as enjoyment, this is one of those shows that you feel like relishing every episode since there's very few in this first season. It could be watched in a day, but it took me much longer because I didn't want it to end. Second season is confirmed on the way though! author: bergars
content: There's basically two fandoms from the same series, fighting over which aspect is better. Oh, the past. The idea that everything's happened, and we can't change it, and the desire to do so can only reign into a meaningless fruit. Now, using the past, as a tool to change the future, beyond the present? I've never seen such a thing. Ripped straight from the bowels of a Nolan movie, combined with the tragedy and drama of life itself. The two camps, the two movies, and both have their strengths; BUT, from what I've seen, people can only pick one. The story began with the sort of premise ... I expected; people doing an emotional job, using time travel to explore the tragedy of the past, while it affects our characters. Those were some OUTSTANDING episodes to blast off. Using the powers from an emotional, realistic standpoint. The vulnerability that comes with knowing too much, and the desire to change it constantly conflicting with the rules of the universe. The mere fact they're using the power for something as small scale as solving people's problems could be a sin. Such a big responsibility, which can only damage the user. That, obviously, creating more of a conflict. “Why shouldn't I change this small little thing?”, well, it could change the entire world for starters. Even after that, and exploring the emotions, and postures of each character, the series turns into a murder mystery. Not a disappointing turn, and actually, it makes much more sense to use the power this way rather than simple, human explorations, but the emotional aspects resonated way more in every way for me. I was disappointed by the shift, and the villain made no sense until the very end. I was a bit confused, a bit frustrated, but I ultimately understand, this is a series that's got more to come. Maybe we'll get some better direction afterward. A focused plot, that doesn't divide quality in places that make the audience fight each other. I want the series to thrive, specially with such a beautiful presentation. Stuffed to the brim with personality, lavishing backgrounds, fluid animation, proper, and interesting camera angles, peak character design, everything to make an extremely solid series with high potential to be something great once it's over. A gateway series into Chinese animation which most people abandon in general. This is one of the best intros to this medium, and I'm excited to see it reach high peaks. 8.4/10. Anything slightly negative I said doesn't remove from the fact I cried hard at some scenes. It's got balls to do the kind of stuff it does.

author: avxry_avx
content: Before I start, I want to preface since some people don't know or understand the difference. This is a DONGHUA NOT ANIME. Donghua is Chinese animation and the differences are NOT just the language but the production and storytelling. Please do not go into this expecting anime lmao, you will not get that. This being a donghua explains the slow start, that a lot of people who didn't like this series hate about it. Donghua, as far as I've seen tend to start off at a slow pace, so you dont get the full picture until like episode 5, however they do go really deep ... later on. Now here is my review: Link Click to me, is possibly one of the best series ever in my honest opinion, but just focusing on Season 1 I can still say its amazing. The animation is just beautiful and both the OP and ED are so fitting and listenable outside of the series, not to forget the incredible direction of the whole story. I currently am studying screen media and film so I value high production and quality direction like this more than anything. I enjoy how the initial first few episodes deceive you a bit into thinking it is just a few short stories about time travel, however all viewers should've at the very least been aware from the get go with how morals and ethics of time travel were being discussed, that this is far more than just some mini mysteries. By the second half of this season, it's fairly obvious this series gets pretty dark, and the more they do and more work they get, the more in deep to trouble they become. By the end of this season you can really see how well thought out every single mystery is, as they all come back to connect to the big picture. I really loved how very slowly there appeared very relevant and important characters, almost without you realising they became significant to the series as a whole, for example Emma and Xiao Li. And on the mention of characters, the main trio are truely great essence to the story. In Season 1 the focus is mainly on the two guys, Lu Guang and Cheng Xiaoshi which their dynamic and teamwork really is showcased through the first season but extends further to what anyone wouldve thought much later on. They're so complimentary to eachother, very directly too. Your typical Yin and Yang dynamic, ig you can interpret that with them how you will. I'd also like to add how their names together Shiguang, means 'Time', a very clever and intentional move with the names alone showing how they rely on eachother to create what they are in the series. Qiao Ling, doesn't know of their business however lets them work without question, she acts in a way as the mediator between the two very contrasting characters, and she holds a lot more importance to the story than whats initially let on. But no spoilers and they dive a lot deeper into her character in Season 2. I really just can't get over how much this series creeps up on you with just about everything, you don't even realise how sentimental or dark it has become really quickly. The mix of psychological, mystery and drama with the tiniest bit of slice of life is just perfect. I love that even if this is a psychological mystery none of it is too far fetched for even the viewers to understand. In series like these its easy for the creators to overcomplicate a mystery to where it no longer makes sense but Link Click does an amazing job. It's so fun to discuss and guess what will happen next, none of it is too predictable but also predictable enough in a way that makes the story make sense. I will always say this is a must watch to anyone with even an inch of critical thinking, please do. My only real critique is how on occasions I was a little lost with some of the characters and mysteries, however by the end it all wraps up really nicely. It's definitely one of the series you really have to finish to even actually give it any sort of judgment. If season 2 didnt exist, I wouldve given this probably a 9/10 but season 2 also just gives season 1 a huge wash of understanding over it. The things that were left to question, were answered and it gave the season another life. Some people might see that as a flaw, but I disagree since it goes to show how they won't rush to the answer or explanation. Link Click will take its time showing us every bit of information rather than a rushed two minute explanation that was pulled out of nowhere, which is what most animes actually tend to do. So now I'll say its a 10/10

author: KC26
content: DO YOURSELF A FAVOUR AND WATCH LINK CLICK! I will keep it spoiler free. Let me start with the concept, the entire plot and the way they built it is amazing. It looks so unique, so fresh, so alluring right from the first episode. It might look like a romance anime from few screenshots but believe me, it's nothing like a rom. It's a hardcore mystery with some classic jump scares and no it's not a horror anime. You get mystery, suspense, thrill, top notch story, one of the best OST's of 2021, and a great immersive experience. I really like how it handled the time travel concept. ... I wondered why did shaking hand time travel in Tokyo Revengers looked dumb but a high five time travel in Link Click looked so awesome. I think the idea behind the power system makes the difference. TR explained nothing and relied heavily on time travel while Link Click handled it perfectly and explained everything gradually with minimum plot conveniences or plot holes. Also, the motivation to time travel is intriguing. It's started as public service and not something as a way to save your loved one. Plus the "Past cannot be changed" was very well executed. I think this is the best time travel concept I've seen in last few years. It has a great sense of realism in it. It's very grounded in general and that makes it even more interesting. The thing that starts as a hard hitting SoL(and believe me I have never seen situations so realistic in animated media ever. It felt like I was watching a story of people I know at all the times) suddenly turns out to be a mind boggling and a well knitted murder mystery with elements of surprise and shock to make it even more interesting. Overall if I had to phrase it in a single sentence, I would say "It's real enough to keep your interest and intense enough to keep you on the edge." Overall a solid 9/10

author: fushiguros_hair
content: This is an anime I wouldn't be ashamed of recommending to someone else. Mostly because there are pretty much no issues with it that I have with most anime (such as unnecessary sexualization of women or out-of-place attraction between characters). Things I liked: Overall, the show consists of different 1-3 episode short stories until the last arc. Each short story was emotional and I enjoyed all of them - they were all very sweet and/or sad. I'm Chinese and it was interesting seeing how accurately episodes portrayed Chinese family dynamics lol, but it made it even sweeter when family members showed how much they cared about ... each other in various episodes. I also liked how there was a strong first episode - I noticed new details after rewatching it. When I first watched it, I was especially glad the plot/characters weren't as predictable as I thought. The first episode was also pretty sad and set the stage for how subsequent episodes would be. Honestly thought it would have implied BL but it's pretty nonexistent. The opening and the ending are a banger! There wasn't much to analyze in the opening or ending though, I think - they just look nice. Also, the OST is pretty good - I love how it's so chill. I was listening to it the other day and half of it is pretty much lofi. There are also some tracks that remind me of emotional moments of the show. I found all of the characters likeable, particularly the main trio - Qiao Ling (the girl with bangs/black hair) has a charisma sometimes that's very cool. There weren't really any one dimensional characters until (mild spoiler) we got to the main (?) antagonist, but I still don't know enough about the antagonist to decide. There are some animation scenes that were great at conveying personalities of characters, such as the CEO in the first episode. Overall, I didn't really have any issues with animation - the art was pretty good. An unrelated note, there's actually a lesbian couple in the second episode and it's done so casually - granted, it's not stated out loud, but it's pretty obvious. It's not sexualized nor does it feel out of place. I was delightedly surprised by this. Things I disliked: There are a few plot gaps, I think. I've rewatched this only once, though. However, there are some reasonable theories for what could've happened in those plot gaps, and they don't interfere a ton with the overall story. I also didn't notice them until I rewatched the show. I watched on funimation and the background music cut out in an important scene in one of the last episodes, which was kind of annoying. Also, in episode 6 or 7, the subtitles lagged behind, which was also kind of annoying. There's one track that sounds a lot like the one punch man theme. It's actually kind of funny.

author: Laila_Vinsmoke
content: (english is not my first language, sorry for the mistakes) ((Instead of calling it "donghua" I’ll call this animation "anime" for the whole review, I hope it’s not offensive)) I started several anime these days, because I wanted something short, but that involved me, nothing too challenging. I’ve tried all kinds and I’ve put most of them on pause. I’ll be honest: I gave this anime a chance for the protagonists, I didn’t read anything about the plot. I started a lot of anime just because I was attracted to some characters (Yarichin B club [...], Haikyuu, JJK and others), but then, no matter how much I loved some ... of them, no one really got me involved, to the point of finishing it in no time. Well. I finished this anime in one day. Usually, to see an 11/12 episode anime takes even a week or at least three days, this makes you understand how much I loved this anime. The plot may seem trivial or obvious or, in any case, very simple at the level of events, but it is simply fantastic as it is structured. Several times my brain froze, no longer understanding what reality was. There are some interesting paradoxes and you don’t understand if that’s reality or a parallel universe, you can’t understand, if there wasn’t Xiaoshi, what would have happened? If no one had seen it, how would certain things have gone? If he had not changed the past, what would the future be like? Maybe it’s just me, is my first anime like this, that I get excited about these things, but I remained anxious and waiting for many episodes, arriving, in some moments, to not understand anything anymore. The ending then is so positively confused, you don’t expect anything to happen and there is this final plot twist that makes you, again, doubt everything you’ve ever seen. I read that maybe there will be a second season, and I’m really curious since now, considering what happened to Guang, their "magic" can no longer be realized, only in half. Leaving aside the plot, which is a 10/10, I would like to dwell for a moment on the characters, the two protagonists. Their relationship is healthy and very beautiful, the difference in their characters is fantastic and the respect and friendship they have for each other is underlined several times, especially in the first episode and in the penultimate. I have no interest in a possible romantic involvement between the two, so don’t misunderstand what I’m going to say now, but they seem to work together. One is calm, serious and professional in what he does; he looks as a neutral spectator and without emotions, as if he were a robot. While the other is sensitive, impulsive and, in their travels, is the "human" figure between the two, who moves and acts as a protagonist, who hopes to change, with his kindness, the world. So consistent with what they do in the photographs, so consistent with their characters. The stories that are told are interesting, some are unrelated to others, while others are connected. I admit that I almost cried in the earthquake, I suffered so much, I felt Xiaoshi’s despair and his anger towards Guang after having deluded him. But in the end, Guang had been clear from the very first time he spoke: death is something that you can’t change, no matter how hard you try, and this is sadly realistic even in our lives, that made me think a lot. Finally, to end wonderfully these eleven episodes, this point of their rules is back in the final scene, when Guang allows Xiaoshi to break this rule and let his impulsiveness and humanity act, preventing his coldness from stopping him. It’s a risky choice, which questions the boy’s faith on the three basic rules, thinking maybe there’s a way to change the future. And it’s the ending that throws us in the face that no, death cannot be changed, too many things would change and fundamental timelines would be missing. The weight of this broken rule is seen in the final scene, opening to the viewer, new doubts that he thought he had eliminated and ignored, hoping for a happy ending that, unfortunately, as in real life, does not exist. The only flaw I found in this anime is the lack of explanation of the origin of the two boys' powers. I really want to understand why they have these powers, if they were born with these, how they developed them, why they have them. I hope it will be explained in the future. I wait with curiosity next season and I'm so sorry that there is not a manga or a continuous that I can read. I hope that a second season will soon arrive and that it will be up to it, so that I can comment with the same love and affection. I think this has officially become my third favorite anime.

content: Simply putting, Shiguang Dailiren or Link Click is a show about two guys who work together to go back in time and do according to the requests of the client. The premise is simple but the plot isn't so much. This anime enters the matter directly within 5 minutes of start, without explanation about what is happening at all. It spares you of the technical understanding of the characters and their abilities right away and instead the viewers learn what it's all about by their own most of the time. Now, Its been a while since i REALLY got so into a show's plot. No, really ... Link Click has one of the most ENGAGING plot lines I have hit on. Apart from the plot, the music of this show is PHENOMENAL and is one of the eminent aspects of the show. The third thing I can't stop loving is the art style. The backgrounds are slightly crayony while the characters get the details. It still fits the vibe of the show very well. This show is so well made that it's honestly hard to properly put in words for me personally. Another great aspect of the show is the opening and ending Themes. The OP And Ed are GREAT and fit the vibe and timings perfectly. You just can't stop loving and appreciating them. Now, I really want to talk about the plot more because it just felt so impactful. Most episodes end in bold cliffhangers. The plot is interlinked end to end and season 1 finishes what it started in the beginning. One of the plot lines dwells upon concepts like past regrets and mistakes. The show really makes you enter the scenes yourself. Yet, the plot also offers thrilling and suspense filled moments. For me personally, I think this show will be very memorable to me because of some scenes. Overall if you haven't watched it, I HIGHLY recommend you to do so if you want a good emotional thrill ride. This show was one of the first Chinese animation shows that i got to get into and honestly it turned out to be one of the best shows I've watched to date. Thanks for reading :)
