author: Galvin34
content: This series has been rather fantastic from beginning to end, with a few caveats. I'm hesitant to call these out as "negatives" of the series, as I believe they are a matter of perspective more than something that can be considered a flaw of the series. CHARACTERS 8/10 Namely, the character development is very single minded, focusing almost entirely on the main character, Cheng Xiaoshi. The secondary protagonist, Lu Guang, gains noticeably less focus and development, even though we catch glimpses of his personality and way of thinking often. The main supporting character, Qiao Ling, gains a few moments of insight into her character, priorities and views in life. ... Her relationship with Cheng Xiaoshi also gets touched upon, moreso than Lu Guang's. The rest of the characters have minor roles or are developed episodically, which limits their development but still proves more than sufficient and can leave you relating and empathizing with the characters. This I believe to be the weakest part of the show, although by now means bad. I think the decision they made - focusing mostly on Cheng Xiaoshi - was an excellent choice considering the limited amount of episodes. STORY 9/10 Cheng Xiaoshi has the ability to go back in time to a moment a photo was taken, possessing the person who took it. Lu Guang has the ability to peer into a photo and see a recollection of events through the eyes of the person who took it. Together, they take up various cases procured by Qiao Ling, who owns the apartment where the former two have set up a photo studio. The story is rather simple and to the point. As a fantasy, there are no strict rules set up on the time-travel. As the show goes on, more 'rules' are revealed, as well as the characters discovering how their powers affect the timelines a bit more. Each "dive" back in time is generally it's own self contained story, which is paced wonderfully and acts as a sort of 'slice of life'. Due to a plethora of the episodes focusing on other characters' lives and memories, the main overarching plot is paced more abruptly, utilizing a lot of cliffhangers. Finally, the show does require a decent amount of suspension of disbelief. As this is a fantasy, some things must be left to chance. I would not recommend approaching the show from a sci-fi, rule driven point of view as the show purposefully does not go into detail on this. ART, SOUND 10/10 The art is fantastic and unique. I like the character designs a lot, the backgrounds seem fantastic, certain scenes have unmatched fluidity and quality you wouldn't expect on first glance. The opening and ending look fantastic, especially the hand movements in the opening. The sound was rather good as well. Opening and ending are catchy and memorable, background music can be a bit generic but is always well fitting and of high quality. I had no complaints and found myself watching both the opening and ending in full each time. The voice acting was good from what I could tell, considering my limited experience with shows in mandarin. ENJOYMENT 10/10 I loved every episode, even the 'extra' one. I didn't mind the cliffhangers too much and think the playing for shock value actually worked quite well. The art was a joy to watch and the music a joy to listen to. I liked most of the characters and think they had a sufficient amount of development, given the circumstances of the story. OVERALL 10/10 I would say that the overall enjoyment depends on the person watching. If you're a fan of rule-drive, gripping time-travel stories where every detail must be analyzed and hold up to scrutiny, it may be lower. If you're a fan of series where the characters drive the story and their development is the main goal, it may be lower. If you generally dislike cliffhangers or episodic series and prefer a more to-the-point pacing, it may be lower. For me personally, all three of these were more of a blessing than an issue, and as such, I thoroughly enjoyed the series and would recommend it to anyone.

author: ghostyen
content: **This review is spoiler-free!** Link Click is a really enjoyable show, and a pleasant surprise for me. It's my first time watching a donghua, and it didn't disappoint - if anything, I'd be interested in watching more of them after this. Story & Art: 9/10 The show uses an episodic format for several of its episodes, with others straying from that to focus on a central storyline. Some episodes are better than others for sure, but overall I enjoyed watching every single one. Nearly every episode is set up to end with a thrilling cliffhanger too, which makes this easy to binge (plus the fact that it's only ... 12 episodes long, including the special filler episode). There will probably be instances where you feel confused about what just happened, but this is because the show drip-feeds you important information along the way - this is really cool imo, as opposed to explaining everything as soon as it happens. There are also multiple references to real-life events that I feel do elevate the story. Lastly, I'm a huge fan of the art style, though I think it won't be for everyone. Sound: 10/10 I really enjoyed all the music used in the show. The OP & ED are both great, and the background tracks were solid too and fit the scenes they played in. I found the Chinese voice acting to be really good, and that everyone had a pleasant voice to listen to. Characters: 8/10 The characters were likeable, although don't expect them to be explored and developed in a lot of depth this season - there are still a lot of unanswered questions to be addressed. I still give them an 8, since I don't feel that this detracted from the show at all, as the story feels like it's just getting started. Overall: 9/10 I would definitely recommend to watch at least the first few episodes and get a feel for it, though, don't expect a big sci-fi extravaganza with nonstop action or anything like that - despite the focus on using time travel, Link Click actually feels very grounded and 'human' in the stories it tells and in how it tells them.

author: NatsumeKhun
content: A lot of people will pass this up because it's a Chinese animation. HOWEVER, that's completely their loss because THIS IS AMAZING. AOTY worthy even. The concept of going back into the past to fix things isn't exactly new, it's been done in anime before several times. However the way it's done feels reminiscent of steins gate and violet evergarden. The characters really get you invested right away. There's no nonsense and it gets down to business quickly. We have our 2 main leads which have a very wholesome and cute working relationship and who, despite being polar opposites personality wise help to balance each ... other out and bring out the best in each other. Their dynamic is really interesting (along with their complimentary powers). Then we have our side characters who actually have tonnes of personality and depth to them in comparison to other things I've seen. They all have their own stories which the protagonists try to help with and each time it's been really interesting! I really loved the basketball episode as it felt really fun to watch. There's also a lot of feelsy moments that will make you shed manly tears of joy. THE ANIMATION. The quality does not drop at all. The OP feels like a massive flex of talent and even throughout the show, the characters are so expressive and fluid. As someone whose used to watching lazy animation it's very refreshing to see. The music is a damned banger and fits really well throughout the donghua. They also use several different beautiful songs which again, is not commonly seen in most anime. My only issue was that at times the subtitles would go by too fast for me to keep up, or it felt like parts of the episodes were cut and skipped with janky translations or lack of translations. It's still watchable, but I wonder if this is just an issue on where I watched it (Funimation) or for other watchers in general. Regardless, please don't pass this up because it's Chinese. Please give it a chance!

author: sukaihai
content: After noticing that this donghua was well received I decided to try a few episodes, and found myself pleasantly surprised! I'd recommend giving at least a few episodes a go. STORY/CHARACTERS The show starts out with an episodic case-of-the-week format, the main characters are able to travel to a specific time through photographs and they take on clients that wish to find information or change minor things from the past. The viewer gets bits and pieces from the lives of these people, but never quite enough to satisfy a growing curiosity and attachment to them and their lives. I mean this as a good thing! I was ... continuously touched by the characters, their stories, motivations and loved ones and even cried on a few occasions. We get introduced to the main characters much the same way, by bits and pieces. Even so by the end I found myself particularly fond of them, and this way of enclosing minimal information periodically felt pleasantly organic. I was quite engaged with the story until the very end and while I think there were some odd choices here and there, my suspension of disbelief was never broken. The overarching plot that begins to emerge is maybe a bit under-baked, but not by a whole lot. I can see my opinion changing depending on how the show continues in the next season. ART/SOUND While I found it difficult to get into the contemporary aesthetics of the show which just didn't speak to me personally, I warmed up to it quick enough. The animation however is overall very beautiful and I enjoyed it's personable look. They had used texturing and gradients generously (but tactfully) which made it feel well loved, and only in episodes 5-7 the animation quality noticably dropped. What comes to the sound design, it wasn't remarkable but it was good. It took me a little bit to get behind the OP and it's tiktok-esque dances but by the halfway point of the show I found it catchy. I quite enjoyed hearing the ED when it came on. Otherwise the sound design was fitting, it made tense moments tenser etc. a bit repetitive but not so that it was bothering. Overall an enjoyable thing!

author: BabyGirl06301
content: I'm not even sure how to begin reviewing this because it's one of those series that is both incredible and obsession-inducing, so I can't be critical of it in any meaningful way, but I'm going to try. If I had to compare this series to anything, it would probably Violet Evergarden. It's definitely got the same episodic feel to it, as well as the intense character connections that make it all super emotional. But Shiguang Dailiren is also a mystery that pulls on the same dramatic strings as ERASED. Neither of these comparisons is perfect, but nonetheless, I think they make it clear that this ... series is the combination of the best aspects of both drama and mystery series, all while having an incredible platform to work off of (the photo diving). It's an odd series to me because it doesn't latch the viewer onto the characters explicitly, but it happens through the storytelling. The characters themselves have great personalities, don't get me wrong, but it isn't the development of them that makes the viewer like them--it's how they interact with the story. Because both elements are working in tandem like that, it's super easy to get hooked on Shiguang Dailiren. The story itself was impeccable, if a bit vague, though I imagine that's to serve the function of creating material for the second season. I don't personally think this series will leave you completely confused--which I think is the trademark of a bad mystery--but I do think it's brilliant at leaving just enough blanks for the viewer to play with. That made the watching experience really fun and engaging. As a whole, I think Shiguang Dailiren brilliantly executed everything it wanted to execute and did so while making every episode more tantalizing than the last. Just the shift from the tone and genre at the beginning of the series to what it is by the final episode was done so well and so smoothly that I didn't actually realize it had happened until I reflected on it through this review. It seems like the story is progressing at exactly the pace it was intended to progress, so I'm confident that, moving forward, the second season will only be full of good content and no irrelevant storytelling, just like this first season was. Absolutely watch this series. Period. It's very much worth your time, and I can't imagine you'll walk away any less than in love with it.

author: whiteflame55
content: It was a short season, but this surprised and delighted me. While the various short arcs felt disconnected (especially episode 5.5), the finale really brought the whole experience together as it found ways to intertwine the take-aways from each arc. The show eased us into the fantastical concept with its first two episodes, which felt a little lighter than the rest of the series while hinting at something more sinister and dangerous operating in the background. The show then transitions into a set of episodes that shifts perception both of the characters and the audience. It's not so much that it throws us into the deep end, ... but rather that the aim shifts from trying to acquire something by peeking into the past to trying to reconcile with the past. It's a devastating set of three episodes that is my favorite material from the series so far. The focus on the words unsaid, often leaving us with just how the various recipients respond to those words rather than the words themselves, was powerful and hit harder as the arc came to its natural conclusion. It also gave us some important insights into Cheng Xiaoshi, who struggles with the curse of foreknowledge as he forms connections in the worlds he enters, and the potential pitfalls of his actions as Lu Guang warns him about altering the past. The rest of the season is a run-up to a dramatic conclusion. It's not so much about the focuses of each arc - a child abducted and a girl attacked - but rather on the consequences of either actively trying to intervene or accidentally altering the past. Even good intentions can have terrible consequences. I very much enjoyed how the season came together in the end, even if I think turning this into a more fantastical battle of wits between characters with various abilities ends up taking a little away from the more grounded elements of the show (yes, I recognize how that sounds in a show involving a person who teleports into the past and possess the bodies of others). It's not that it doesn't make sense, especially since the premise of the show involves a similarly fantastical set of elements, but the show does lose a little something by introducing an out-and-out villain into the mix, even if it does lead to a pretty harrowing scene to round out the season. Overall, I think there's a lot to love here. I think I would have liked S1 even more if it had stayed focused on these smaller arcs rather than jumping into the big one by the end, but it's hard to argue with a solid cliffhanger.

author: nein_yards
content: (No spoilers in this review) This anime has really great production quality, with brilliant art, fluid animation, a great premise, as well as killer execution. It's really close to perfect. author: decris-la
content: I never write reviews but I just had to for this show. Where do I even begin? It's such a hidden gem and it's really such a shame that it isn't more popular. Story: 10/10 Right from the very first episode, the story is absolutely phenomenal. It got me hooked and invested right from the get-go. Although time travel isn't by any means a novel concept, I still think that the storyline is very unique, and the photo aspect of it is a very nice touch. There are high stakes and such real, raw emotional plots in almost every episode. It addresses issues like workplace harassment, ... natural disasters, loss and grief, human trafficking, etc. Overall, the storyline is just really great. It's definitely a real tear-jerker. Art: 9/10 The art and animation are also amazing. It's a unique style, but refreshing. The character designs are nice, and I really like the ambiance of the backgrounds/lighting. The art style is quite pleasing to look at and it's well done. The intro animation is also very unique. Sound: 10/10 The MUSIC. The soundtrack for this donghua is absolutely AMAZING. I don't think I've skipped the intro or the ending a SINGLE time, which I've never done for any other anime. Both the OP and ending are absolute bangers. However, the rest of the soundtrack is equally as good, even the instrumental. This show is filled with amazing songs that compliment the story very well. Characters: 8/10 Personally, I love the characters, but I will admit that some of the characters besides Cheng Xiaoshi do fall a bit flat in terms of deeper development, and it's likely a consequence of only having 11 main episodes. However despite this, the characters are still very likable and entertaining, even the side characters, and I find myself getting attached to their stories and struggles (especially Emma </3). Overall enjoyment: 10/10 Overall, I really enjoyed this show and it was a very refreshing change of pace compared to other shows airing at the moment. It was nothing short of amazing, and each and every episode had me at the very edge of my seat. It's definitely now one of my favorites and I can't wait for season 2.

author: Rixku
content: I think Shguang Dailiren is probably one of my favorite anime for this season or perhaps maybe the whole year. I'm upmost surprised that the writer actually found a way to make everything connect in this story, since at first it all seems a bit unusual and random. The main cast of characters in this anime, I quite like ... them a lot. Usually, in the main cast, I would find at least one character a bit irritating; however, I personally don't find it a problem in this one. The arts style and animation is quite nice and can be distinguished by others especially with how the eyes are drawn (which I so adore). The scenes fit perfectly with each other and the designs of the characters are simple and easy to differentiate from. What actually made me watch Shiguang Dailiren in the first place was the opening animation and the song (Dive Back in Time by Bai Sha JAWS) that went with it. The hand movements that go with the melody is always so entertaining to watch, making is un-skippable unlike some other anime intros. Speaking about the songs for the opening and ending, I think some genius conducted the way with how scenes can easily fade in and out with the opening and ending... They always seem to find a way to have the ending episode match the mood of the ending song (Overthink by Fan ka) which I always find so amazing! One moment they got me crying my eyes out- then the next second they got me jamming to the song which I can never skip. This anime may I say it again, is probably one of my favorites and I cannot express my sincere appreciation of taking time to watch it; for it always takes me on the edge of my seat.

author: paranoid_soul
content: An absolute hidden gem, but masterpiece it is not. Link Click is yet another one of the works that rest on the arguably overused time travel premise. Works that explore this theme usually have trouble explaining away plot holes and inconsistencies, and Link Click is no exception. It is not yet explained clearly how physics in Link Click works. How many time flows are there? It seems as if there is only one, since the MCs are careful not to influence the time flow. Like other time travel works, there are link events (?) that, if changed, can alter the whole timeline. But how do ... they alter the flow? Do they create an alternate timeline, meaning that two timelines could exist where a link-action was taken and one where it was not (multiverses)? Or do they just simply change this unique time flow? How are link-events determined anyway? Why does Lu Guang know which events are life-changing but Xiaoshi doesn't? This seems pretty important -- shouldn't Lu Guang give him a brief on time-travel physics before? Although the characters repeatedly assure the viewers that they did not dare to change link-events for fear of affecting the future, it seems that the future is the way it is because they travel into the past. So what does this all mean? Does it mean whatever they do during time -travel will not change the future anyway, since their time-traveling has already been determined and reflected in the present they are residing in? Furthermore, what happens to the person whose mind is heisted? Do they forget everything, or do they form new memories? Since it is not technically *their* mind, I assume they just forget everything, because it seems like the hosts are all confused upon waking up. But this also isn't right, because there is one episode where a client asks them to convey a message to his friends and family. If he can't remember passing the words, then what's the point? Perhaps my criticism of the plot can be explained away, for I am losing braincells writing this review. Wrapping one's head around a time-travel story is always excruciating, so forgive me. To explore time travel, Link Click uses the mind-heist trope, a trope that has been employed by critically acclaimed movies such as Inception and Possessor. The series, however, does introduce photo-diving as a means to travel through time, something I have yet to see before. This addition to the trope is notable, but nothing particularly praise-worthy since it is not incredibly creative. I appreciate Link Click's emphasis on photographs as our life montages: they are reminders of our pasts and thus, a part of our life and identity. Accordingly, the series's first few episodes are episodic in nature, each displaying a new life story. These episodes were touching, and the director did a great job making the viewers attached to the new characters although they only appear for one or two episodes. There are some moments that are hard to believe here and there, such as when a client's friends' family start fighting each other although he is trying to warn them about an imminent earthquake (like who do that? Someone is telling you you have 1 hour to live, and instead of trying to confirm the information, you fight among yourselves), but I think I am being nit-picky. These episodic episodes, however entertaining they are, distract us from the bigger picture: where is this heading to? I know from the first episode that there is a serial killer on the loose, and that the main characters are probably going to solve it, but the intermission makes me forget about it until the topic is raised again in the series. The last two episodes were suspenseful, but there was not really a twist like many viewers say. The so-called twist should be obvious to any experienced viewer. This twist also bends the genre to action/thriller/supernatural completely, which renders the slice-of-life intermission redundant in my opinion. In terms of characters, yes, the characters are flat. The only more developed character is the main character, Xiaoshi. However, unlike many other critics, I don't think this is necessarily a fault, since this is only season 1. As long as the other characters are not annoying (like cough cough Demon Slayer cough), I am willing to overlook this. The sound design is great. The soundtracks are absolute bangers, but unfortunately, the selection is small. I hear only two background music tracks: a light-hearted one, and a suspenseful one. The episodes almost always follow the same formula: light-hearted music plays, a client comes, Xiaoshi jumps inside the picture, messes up, and then *insert that one suspenseful music*. At some point, when that one suspenseful music started to play, I sighed out of ennui. What truly stands out is the breathtaking art and animation. You feel like you're watching a Ghibli movie in lo-fi mode. I have no words to describe the art. It is just simply perfect. The colors, the palette, the style, everything! The voice acting is not

Now let’s get to the good stuff. author: reveriehina
content: Link Click is one of those rare series that quietly starts off simple but gradually pulls you into something emotionally devastating, beautifully written, and deeply human. At its core, the story follows two protagonists who enter photographs to relive moments from the past. What seems like an interesting supernatural concept quickly becomes something much heavier — exploring regret, loss, trauma, and the irreversible nature of time. What makes this series stand out isn’t just its unique premise, but how grounded it feels emotionally. Every case they take on carries real weight, and the storytelling never feels rushed or superficial. It’s the kind of anime that makes you ... sit in silence after an episode ends. The animation is clean and expressive, especially during emotional scenes where subtle facial expressions do most of the storytelling. The soundtrack also deserves praise — it knows exactly when to stay quiet and when to hit you emotionally. If you’re looking for something fast-paced and light, this is not it. But if you want something that will stay in your head long after you finish it, Link Click delivers. Link Click is not just a story about time travel — it’s a story about grief, consequences, and emotional acceptance. It’s beautifully written, painfully human, and unforgettable. Highly recommended for anyone who wants an emotionally impactful experience.

Things eventually go into more serious territory with higher crimes, cases, and even murders. I absolutely loved the series, what with it's storytelling, excellent characters. insane plot twists, and the emotional baggage it leaves on you. The other thing that the anime is not afraid ... to show is, not only about how we can't change the past, and one can't change the past from the butterfly effect, but also about the heavy-weighted topics we wish we could change, however, in the long run, they eventually mean something bigger. In the end of the show, they leave the viewer absolutely hungry for more with season two with amazing plot devices, abilities, and plot twists. Also, the soundtrack is absolutely amazing. Because of its short number of episodes, I recommend this to everyone, especially if you love a good mystery show - it'll blow your doors clean off its hinges.

author: Esperanta
content: This is 1/175 of trying to watch every single Time Travel anime on MAL Link Click, where do I start on this. This show is amazing, personally. It has everything I could ever ask for in a show. There's a great story, likable heroes, and a brilliant concept, and is the show that inspired me to start this series. What it's about ------------------ Link Click is about 2 best friends, Cheng Xiaoshi and Lu Guang, who use their special powers to run a shop called the "Time Photo Studio" Where they fulfill clients requests to go back in time and do stuff such as easing regrets and solving mysteries ... from the past. Cheng Xiaoshi and Lu Guang each have different powers. Cheng Xiaoshi is able to travel back in time using a photo, possessing the person who took the photo at that exact time. Lu Guang is able to share conciousness with Cheng Xiaoshi, acting as a guide so that Cheng Xiaoshi doesn't mess up the timeline or do anything too risky. What I Liked --------------- I liked a lot, like the characters for example. Cheng Xiaoshi and Lu Guang are very likable protagonists, and they each play an equally important role in the story. They also live with a girl named Qiao Ling, who provides more dynamics to the place. The way they interract with eachother is so fun and it feels like they are all actual friends. The story is also a highlight, this show is filled with happy moments, sad moments, funny moments, and you never seem to know what they will pull off next. It even has a few action sequences, one of them (I wont spoil here) being done really creatively, which was brilliant and something I would have never thought of before. The OP and EP are really good, and the soundtrack has some of the best songs i've ever heard in a show, with my personal favorite for this season being "Power". The animation is really nice too. Theres so many details that I love about this show. What I Disliked ------------------- Honestly there is nothing I really disliked about this. The only thing really is there is a bunch of cliffhangers, so don't expect being able to put it down easilly. Overall -------- Super fun show, the characters are great, the concept is great, if your looking to get into time travel shows this is my personal top choice.

author: TwixxieRoll
content: Tackling a time travel concept? It's like playing with fire. Time travel is one of the hardest concepts to pull off because of all the rules and massive areas for plotholes. When done well, it becomes almost flawless and squeaky-clean in terms of leaving loose ends, see: Steins;Gate, which is my favorite anime of all time. Link Click has undertaken a unique concept of carrying out this time travel element, in that the past cannot be changed no matter what, as opposed to the more popular ones which mostly centers around characters going back in time to change a certain thing. This led to several conflicts ... of interest between the two lead characters, the executor, Chen Xiaoshi, being the more emotional character; while the guide, Lu Guang is the more pragmatic and rational one. It was very interesting to see the characters communicate while carrying out their tasks, and what really drew me in is the fast-paced stories and enticing storyline. We also see the most basic time travel concept of the "butterfly effect" really coming into play and being the key feature in this donghua. This series is extremely binge-able because it is very fast-paced and easy to follow. However, it does have some melodramatic moments that are a little emotionally manipulative and cringe for my liking. The ambiguous ending really leaves a lot of questions unanswered, which hopefully will be addressed in season 2.

author: nigelpun
content: A suspensful show where the main character is forced to face a harsh reality. The story focuses on mini stories because they are a detective agency. While I think the characters are written well, one of their characters get significantly more focus than the other even though it seems they should be almost equals. I'm sure when the second season is released the director will balance it out. The art is unique from ... anime and beautifully drawn in the style of Chinese manhua. The soundtrack is also different from the majority of anime. The majority are all symphony recordings but this has a mixture of different genres. I watched this one for the plot and excellent character writing. This isn't a coming of age anime. The characters are working class adults which is why it makes sense that they've already developed their own values and it's interesting to see how different perspectives tackle an issue. author: Tery1015
content: Tl;dr; It's an Intricate, intense and suspenseful show. Definitely one of the best Chinese anime in my book and best psychological anime. Story The anime’s episodes are told semi episodically, with individual arcs accumulating into a grander plot. This is done well because the build up is intense as the show progresses over time. The story becomes a lot more complicated and the stakes get higher as the effects of altering past events begin to spiral into more issues that will come back to bite the protagonists with every event in the past that they fiddle with. Link Click does, however, borrow a few concepts; time travel ... and its implications and with huge consequences for each decision the duo takes. But the execution is a lot better compared to similar time manipulation themed anime. The show paces itself really well, allowing flowing transitions of tense moments, to more heartfelt moments, to more light hearted moments, without feeling too cheesy (there is some cheese, the show does bring numerous tearjerker scenes, such is the case when involving almost every person the main characters help). That being said the anime paces itself well and hits you with gigantic cliffhanger after gigantic cliffhanger episodically, which definitely draws viewers in. Now this show does appear to have more to offer as the initial episodes hint at more to come, for now though it's very satisfying to see just how this time travelling thriller progressed. The only possible issue I still hold on to is the logic behind the mechanics of time travel. The anime gives exposition to how it works initially, though the rules do seem to change and the logic of the change isn't always as water tight in preventing plot holes. Still a great story in the end. Art The show’s production looks pretty slick and high quality. If I was to pick features I liked in the production it would be the touch realism that the landscape and objects have in this anime. From simple things like phones, basketball courts, to streets. It all looks sooo good and feels so urban. The art is pretty consistent for the most part. Sound It’s a Chinese anime, so of course the accent and general voice and tone of the characters feels different from Japanese voices. This took time for me to adjust to but eventually it all good because the characters still had souls in them. Like they still had their respective emotions, and tone still felt appropriate after getting used to it. Chinese voices obviously add their own distinct phrases and expressions, but I figure the subs mediate for that so that viewers aren’t lost, I didn’t feel lost. Onto the Soundtrack, the opening and ending to the anime was slick and upbeat, helping the urban tone in the anime. The background ost held up well enough, not extremely well or anything. Characters The main 3 Main Characters are a good driver of the story. All the decisions they make drive the stories. Without really going into describing each of them, I’ll say that they complimented each other well. The side characters who come for help with past events they want to alter each bring their own sense of resonance as to things people wish they changed and unhappiness people possess in the current. Overall I enjoyed this show very much, I did not expect to but I did. There were times where things felt too over emotional and pretentious, however this won't deter how well made this show is and how it may just be one of the best psychological time travel anime out there.

author: Elhwing
content: I just finished watching Shiguang Dailiren, also known as Link Click, and I'll try to explain in this review why I think this show is an interesting one. You can jump to the TL;DR at the end of this review if you want a concise summary. The story : It involves time travelling and solving mysteries. You'll get into the story rather easily, and that's one of the show's main strengths : the plot isn't overcomplicated, but it remains captivating : some scenes are quite thrilling, there are a few cliffhangers and you'll be eager to start the next episode as soon as possible. There are ... some emotionnal scenes, and to be honest, it felt like they worked better than in other animes, it's as if we could really understand the struggle felt by characters. The characters : One might say that they aren't that original and that's kind of true. However, they all have their distinct personality, and the relationship between the main characters is original enough. But don't expect anything incredible, the characters are lovable and you'll like the main ones, but the show isn't innovative in that regard. The soundtrack : Close to perfection ( btw you can find the whole soundtrack on youtube ), many different songs that fit very well the scenes and enhance the watching experience overall. The opening & ending songs are great aswell, some people criticize the opening's visuals because they are a bit out of place in comparison with the show, but it's not really relevant, it won't prevent you from enjoying the song nor the anime. The animation : I won't get technical here, simply because I lack the knowledge to write about it, but the visuals are good looking, and it's refreshing to watch a show that relies on different techniques/designs than what you'll usually find in japanimation. The reason why I didn't rate it 10/10 : Although I've already said that the story's simplicity has many pros, it does have some cons. I won't spoil anything, but let's say that the show might be a bit too generous with the rules it established regarding the whole time travelling thing, therefore it can feel like the show is "cheating" its way out. There's nothing wrong with the plot not being heavily focused on precise explanations ( as a matter of fact, many shows have a hard time giving flawless details etc... ) but it does hurt a bit its coherence. TL;DR : Shiguang Dailiren is a thrilling show : it's a balanced mix between action, suspense, emotions, involving believable characters. The story isn't hard to follow, however, it will sometimes feel a bit too convenient at times. We can qualify this fact by remembering that time travelling shows are almost always a mess when it comes to giving "logical" explanations. Anyhow, the few plotholes are far from unbearable, and the qualities of this show are far bigger than its few flaws, I highly recommend it to anyone, even people who aren't usually attracted by time travelling, because Link Click is closer to a sol show than a sci-fi one.

author: Brightly_Lit
content: It is very, very rare that I would ever declare a show perfect or give it 10 stars, but here we are. I would also give Darker Than Black season one 10 stars, 86, maybe Spy x Family season one, probably My Hero, a few others, but of truly great shows that illustrate the full potential of the medium, Link Click season one is among the very best. The animation is spectacular, opening themes are fantastic for both seasons, characters are deep and real and intriguing. Like Darker Than Black, most of season one tells stories in pairs of episodes. Unlike Darker Than Black, or any ... show I've ever seen, these seemingly unrelated smaller stories build upon one another, finally coming around full circle ouroboros style to brilliantly reconnect the final episode with the first. Our heroes, Lu Guang and Cheng Xiaoshi, each have powers that make it possible to, working together, dive into the body of the person who took a photo. In addition to a regular photomat,they run a side business diving into photos for the customer. Maybe a customer wishes they said something they didn't in the past. Maybe they're trying to solve a mystery, or find their child. Each of the stories is deeply moving, as is how profoundly living in these other bodies and taking on their lives affects the impulsive Cheng. He thinks it'll be no big deal to just get in there, do the job, and get out, but he always gets drawn in, and struggles to follow the far more serious Lu's instructions on what he mustn't change - since, as all the time travel stories say, the butterfly effect could change their present catastrophically. Lu seems to speak from painful experience. There are hints of some great sacrifice Lu made for Cheng in the past that led to their present situation, maybe even forced Cheng into almost an indentured servant role working this way with Lu, but even by the end of season two, there is almost no concrete information about it; it remains a tantalizing mystery. Heck, if you just want to watch a couple of hot guys have an unusually ~entwined~ relationship, you could use this show that way. In addition to being all about modern technology (people continually taking selfies definitely makes their jobs easier) and hip to modern life, the show is well aware of what many people are looking for in their anime, and it delivers: Lu and Cheng's relationship is (subtly) ripe for fanfic. Also, as an aside, I've gotta give the show kudos for being The. Only. Show. that doesn't hand - wave implausible stuff. This is the only show where you won't have to ever say, "Why didn't he just do this or that?" or, "That's what cell phones are for," or, "What about that one thing?" The show is aware of all these things and will address them, so you never have to suspend disbelief extensively; for a show about something so fantastical, it's highly realistic. There are things that may make it harder for someone to get into than most anime. This is a Chinese show, and though season two is well translated, season one ... isn't. Some of it seems very much like the original dialogue was entered into Google translate and they just used whatever came out, but with a little effort to try to figure out what's being said, it can be done, and it's so, so worth it. Similarly (though all too commonly), anything written is not translated, and sometimes it's quite important, but you can nearly always get it from context, or if you're desperate, you can look it up online. Hopefully a better translation will be given to this season; I feel surely that would have to help it be more successful among English speakers. I literally can't recommend this show enough; it's one of the greatest things I've ever seen. I'm so glad it was made.

author: joemaamah
content: This is one strong donghua, and is definitely a worthy entry in adult animation. It starts out kind of slow, and I thought it was going to be purely an episodic adventure. But it's not. The writers spend the first half of the season doing a fantastic job setting up, and foreshadowing, what happens in the 2nd half and beyond. If you like good writing, Link Click has it in abundance. The artwork is solid and I found it quite pleasing. This might have the best animation of any Chinese production, although it isn't off-the-chain action packed. Still, it is very quality rendered, without a lot ... of the cost cutting measures you see in other Chinese animation. At first I raised an eyebrow over the characters. They didn't initially make much sense. But as noted, the writers took their time setting them up. As the series moves along, they come into sharper and sharper focus. Eventually I found they made perfect sense, based on their past, present, and future, experiences. It's so hard to not jump the shark with time travel shows, but this one is nicely done. It shows the writers put some thought, time and effort into the results and consequences of the characters' choices. Very little slips by, in the long run. These writers certainly deserve kudos for a job well done. A very able English VA cast makes a big difference here. They were well directed, too. As was mentioned, this series could have easily jumped the tracks, but everything was pulled together in a masterful way. This title is a snapshot of superb. If I was grading it, I'd give it a 95/100 for a solid A. I don't often do this, but if you make it through the first season I can't recommend watching the 2nd season enough. It's even better, as it pulls all the pieces together into a congruent whole. You COULD just watch the first season, and let it go at that. But you'd be sorely shortchanging yourself. Click on it

author: lamaraptor
content: An unexpected instant masterpiece in the anime world, and it didn't even come from Japan. From the very first minute it becomes so engaging learning how these time travel powers work and watching the poignant and sometimes outright tragic stories unfold in the photos of various people's lives. Such a fresh and wholly original idea and executed so beautifully it's no wonder this one has been generating a lot of buzz, and a lot of hype for a second season. At first it can seem very episodic in nature, each episode acting as an isolated narrative delving into a single person's life and revealing some of ... the uglier parts of humanity but also showing how the bonds we make with others shape our happiest moments. But it becomes clear as it goes on there's an underlying story yet to be told and there's still a lot of mystery in the air surrounding our protagonists, their powers, and what this is all leading to. Personally I would give this a 10/10 with no reservations just on the strength of the intrigue it's been able to build over these 11 episodes, but I'm going to have to wait to hold off on giving it that perfect score. This is obviously an unfinished story and it's very possible for them to drop the ball if they aren't able to deliver satisfying answers to a lot of the questions they've raised. I for one can't wait to see what's in store and I'm optimistic for how it'll all turn out. 9/10

(Also the time travel is interesting and has creative uses in the later episodes but gets a big middle finger in Season 2, which I'm not happy about, the laws are also pretty confusing as the characters can but somehow can't do anything they want in the past?! Season 2 again does clear this up by saying you CAN do anything you want but it'll just mess up the timeline but sometimes it doesn't so what's the limit here?! Concept was interesting but fell flat upon execution) The OP is semi-cringe but bearable and the ED absolutely rocks. Link Click does use a lot of melodrama in the early episodes to get the viewers interested in its concept of time travel (only to completely disregard it in the second season). The music is intrusive at times and sometimes doesn't match the vibe, taking away from the experience. HOWEVER, I enjoyed the hell out of it. The art is gorgeous, the episodes fly by like crazy. The twists and cliffhangers are insane and the last 4 episodes are absolutely lit. If you're the emotional type, the early episodes might evoke a few tears and then you completely forget what was going on and get invested in the main plot. Season 2 ROCKS, and it's why you should watch the first. If you want a great popcorn muncher while not wanting some deep or dark stuff, this is the show for you. TLDR; Great show with top tier twists and cliffhangers but to manage expectations its by no means a masterpiece, if you really want a stellar time travel show go watch Steins;Gate instead but if you just want something nice and simple go watch Link Click A 10/10 enjoyment rating but it's really nothing else. Works better as a murder mystery compared to a time travel show.

author: ST63LTH
content: TL;DR: This is a wuxia cultivation series that doesn't have BL and has an actually good plot, great animation, detail and sound design as well as consistent character development. Mortal's Journey is a Chinese wuxia donghua that follows Han Li, a child of a poor village family who sacrifices himself to enter the seven mysterious sect in order to improve his family's living situation. Unfortunately he fails the entrance exam but is accepted as a medic's disciple learning medicine and the path of cultivation. He encounters trauma when he finds his medic teacher Mo is not what he seems and his disciple friend who showed ... no affinity to cultivation suddenly changing his path of cultivation to martial arts. This story is goes very in depth with character establishment in the beginning which almost made me drop it but I'm glad that I stuck along. Story: 9/10 I still consider this to be a somewhat overpowered main character, he has inept affinity to cultivation and has mastered medicine and potential for cultivation based on his Teacher Mo's literature. Han Li's journey is littered with small fry antagonists that get destroyed but the story stays true to development by sticking to a lower scale of characters. Art & Sound: 9/10 The art is literally amazing. I haven't seen CGI this detailed and colorful ever. I think the characters are motion captured because the body movements and facial movement are so realistic even the minute details like wrinkles are shown in the characters faces. The color is well informed, in many scenes we see the animators have implemented 3 point lighting. For example, in Episode 4 (9:33) we see on Teacher Mo there are 2 aspects of 3 point lighting (rim light provided by ambient light from the windows facing away from the sun and fill light provided by active light probably supplied by the sun) this detail in lighting makes the art and animation more enjoyable. Furthermore, the action scenes aren't just static fast motion follow focused shots. They are dynamic and unpredictable which also adds into the action. The focus changes in some shots where spears are thrown out of hand or when an opponent lunges forward toward MC or friendly characters. Furthermore, the specific shot types are well informed, I even spotted a dolly zoom in one of the shots where Han Li visits the Mo mansion on a bridge (I think that scene) which was a surprise. The sound is also surprisingly excellent, the music reflects the mood and in cases of action scenes the music is often suspenseful which reminds me of well choreographed action/drama K-dramas. Although they are very suspenseful and reflect the mood well, it isn't a memorable experience because there aren't any theme songs. Character: 8/10 Character development is the most apparent in the first half of Season 1, we are introduced to the main cast in the first episode which is a thrust into the story. I wished they didn't have a storytelling beginning that shows MC's past because it feels like a waste of having it in third person. It would have been better to not know Han Li would become an immortal yet because the beginning is confusing. The montage with a proper time scale contributed to Han Li's character training arc by condensing all the good parts instead of wasting 1 hour on forced development. This was a fairly good call to make considering the detail and quality this season had to set. At the moment, there aren't any love interest connections which is a letdown because I keep feeling this is a Shounen Ai type story. Although, the meeting of Teacher Mo's daughter and Han Li seemed a bit promising, I doubt anything will progress in that direction in terms of love interest. Overall: 9/10 Subjectively and Objectively this is a good watch. There is a lot at stake on this series as they have maximized the detail and quality they could bring in terms of plot, art and sound as well as character development. Highly recommended, I enjoy overpowered main characters but I also enjoy rational, zero to hero cultivation stories where every episode isn't a new enemy but a progress to cultivation. Very philosophical.

author: AntyVerse2021
content: I'll be honest: this is my first experience with Chinese 3D animation. I decided at some point in some day of some month of some year to diversify my repertoire and see what people from the country of Winnie the Pooh can create. Especially as I have not had much exposure to Chinese pop culture in my life, at least not to the same extent as Japanese pop culture. Here, of course, we are not counting creations i.e. the poor remake of Mulan from Disney or the concentration camps for Uighurs. So how did Fanren Xiu Xian Chuan fare after that huge number of reviews ... on MAL, four in number while writing this in 2024, of A Record of a Mortal Journey to Immortality? It was just meh. Like a big MEH. STORY 5/10 Let's start with the story: a poor kid joins the minor sect (that doesn't sound at all like an introduction to a psychological horror film with a theme of reliving trauma) and so soon begins his story towards immortality, surviving along the way... moderately interesting adventures. Let's start with the most important thing: the story is boring and seems to be going nowhere for most of this season. In the sense, we know that the main character wants to achieve immortality, so along the way he walks into a parade of various bad guys, defeats them, occasionally acquires some piece of equipment from them or another superpower, which makes him stronger, and that's about it. Only towards the literal end do we get some interesting plot expansion and foreshadowing of some interesting conflict. Before that, the first half of the show with the Wolf Gang resembles a half-baked side quest from Fallout: New Vegas that you want to complete mainly for the extra EXP. And this sentence is a great insult to NV, because at least there was something worth remembering from Goodsprings. The conflict itself is just resolved crudely, without any life. Overall, the whole world in this donghua seems lifeless and it's not about the graphics, we'll get to that part later. Some people in the reviews praised this work for some philosophical message, and it made me spit on my monitor laughing as I was drinking tea. There is as much depth here as in a dried up puddle. To be clear: not every story has to have a profound message. Sometimes an idiotic action movie is just what our monkey brain needs after a hard day's work. But saying that Fanren Xiu Xian Chuan's first season has some deep message is like saying that 365 Days is the pinnacle of Polish romantic cinema without having seen any Polish film before. I complain about the plot all the time, but I'd be lying if I said it was something entirely bad. It does have some interesting moments, I particularly liked showing that life and the system aren’t always fair, even when you work very hard. It wasn't anything special, but it was nice to see. And as I said: the ending shows some seeds of an interesting conflict, but I was simply bored on the whole. GRAPHICS 7/10 The universe likes balance, so it's time for me to praise this ONA for something. The 3D graphics look just fine. It's not some work of art, but the particle effects and the whole thing looks good, it certainly could have been worse. The only time it really looks bad is when the camera zooms in on a character's eyes, it then looks like someone is putting their hand up their arse to use them as a puppet. It is also lazy to use real-world photos or video, but this is rare enough that complaining about it starts to border on being petty. What I must commend, however, are the fights. These look genuinely good, even if they sometimes resemble PS3 cutscenes. And it was a nice change seeing completely fluid combat, from the usual turn-based combat of most anime. The fights themselves have nice choreography, the characters fly coolly, continuing the glorious Chinese tradition of being suspended from ropes, varied with various magical abilities and weapons, in that respect it's the full package. CHARACTERS 3/10 Know what? The plot really doesn't have to be anything particularly good or deep. Sometimes it's enough for the characters to be easy to like and memorable. Well, you guessed it from the rating that A Record of a Mortal Journey to Immortality contains some really 'fascinating' characters to get to know. I'm really trying to recall any characterisations of the main character. Han Li is such a white piece of paper that if the number of character elements were converted to the amount of fat in the body he would be bloody anorexic. If the same process was applied to the rest of the cast we would be left with a skeleton crew. Authentically I am able to say more about Bell from Danmachi, Kirito from SAO, heck, even the main character of OniAi than I can about Li Han. I've seen pieces of titanium that were less stiff than the protagonist of this series. As for the rest of the characters: by some miracle it is even worse. Apart from the characters from the first half, no one is worth remembering, and the interesting ones just disappear aft

author: HouseOfCards
content: This is a Chinese animation (donghua) so some people might be hesitant but it's really good. I would recommend it if you are into adventure stories with low-key smart MC's that aren't OP that don't constantly have crazy fight scenes. I got started with Tales of Demons and Gods, and watched a few others, but this is probably one of the best ones out there. This is a typical cultivation story with the MC starting out weak in ancient times and progressively getting stronger, but the story always has a degree of realism. One of my biggest qualms about donghua is usually the unrealistic MC ... who can do everything and overcome any obstacles by growing OP quickly, but as people, we cannot. This MC is always aware of the ever present danger of life and he has to constantly make tough but practical decisions. He's very relatable and the story pulls you into the world. The MC is average and just in a world trying to survive and get stronger. He devotes himself to his cultivation and lives secretively, knowing that those who stick out get attacked. It's an adventure, exploring the cultivation world where there's danger everywhere and lots of mystery and wonder. In addition to cultivation, there's magic, special weapons, and formations, all of the typical cultivation world stuff. He's initially the son of a poor family whose parents have to sell one of their children to have enough to eat. From a young age, he overheard his parent's talking about it and volunteered himself to protect his sister. He gets sold into a sect where he gets a preview to the cultivation world with a test where it's survival of the fittest to get into it as a cultivator as opposed to just doing odd jobs. The art is elegant. Sometimes I forget its an animation but other times the animation looks pretty fake, but better than most donghua and some anime. The music really fits the mood and intro and outro are enjoyable but nothing to go crazy over. Overall, it's a good show with realistic struggles to survive day to day, not really an OP MC. There is a lot of world building but also a lot of mystery. You're learning about the world along with the MC, but it doesn't feel fake like the author tries to add stuff along the way to help the plot. That said, the pacing can be considered moderate or slow, the main plot can get sidetracked sometimes. There's a bit of life philosophy and struggle. I enjoyed it as it wasn't a show I had to turn my brain off nor did I have to think too much. It is an adventure.

author: daylilyyy
content: Fanren Xiu Xian Chuan is a standout donghua for fans of strategic. If you like smart, slow-burn cultivation stories with a clever hero, this donghua is worth watching. The start is slow, but it gets much better. It follows the journey of Han Li, an ordinary mortal who enters the world of cultivation through wit, perseverance, and caution. The donghua has gained attention for its unique protagonist and cultivation realism, but it also has some notable weaknesses. This donghua is great because it has a smart main character (Han Li) who uses his brain instead of just fighting. The world feels real and dangerous, where cultivators must ... be careful to survive. While the animation starts rough, it gets much better later with cool fights and nice visuals. The story is great that stands out in the xianxia genre.  Unlike many stories with super powerful heroes, this one shows a more realistic journey with challenges and smart planning On the negative side, The show starts slow, which might test your patience at first. The animation in early episodes feels stiff and awkward before improving later. While Han Li gets good development, most side characters don't get enough depth to make you care about them. The story stays serious all the time, missing those fun moments that could lighten the mood. Also, if you're new to cultivation stories, some parts about power systems and politics might confuse you at first.

author: ninja35mm
content: Score: 11/10 — One of the rare gems Like many of you, I don't have a huge list of anime that I can truly call my favorites. Fanren Xiu Xian Chuan isn’t a “classic” in the traditional sense, but somehow, it managed to become one of those rare 11/10 shows for me. So, what’s the protagonist like? He’s humble yet brave, calculating but kind, clever but never deceitful. If I had to point out a flaw (as of Season 6), it’s probably that he’s a bit too distant when it comes to romance — especially with the women around him. But honestly, it fits his character and ... journey. The story? It’s classic cultivation at its best — full of intense battles, steady progression, and stunning, breathtaking animation. There’s a constant sense of movement and momentum, and you can feel the stakes growing higher with each arc. Yes, there’s humor. Yes, there’s tragedy. But most importantly, there’s always a challenge. The protagonist never feels overpowered — he’s constantly pushed to his limits, and watching how he overcomes each obstacle is absolutely gripping. The only real drawback might be the animation of character movements. Sometimes it lacks realism or fluidity, especially in earlier seasons. But the studio is clearly improving with each episode. You can feel the evolution not just in the story, but in the production quality too. And honestly, the animation style they’ve chosen comes with its own trade-offs — it may not allow for perfect realism, but it delivers in scale, flair, and atmosphere. If you're into cultivation stories, this donghua deserves a spot on your watchlist. You might not expect much at first — but give it time. It might just become one of your unexpected favorites too.

author: HenriqueNeves
content: The greatest potential of Chinese anime (donghua) recently released - mainly by the producers Bilibili and Tencent Penguin Pictures - comes from a great expressive use and enabling its 3D. While many are still prejudiced against this language - relatively recent considering that it is less than 50 years since its emergence - which is still undergoing great development, it seems to me that it has reached maturity at Pixar. But that does not prevent that animes like "Douluo Dalu, 2018" and "Ling Long: Incarnation, 2019" have been able to use this resource in a very evident, expressive and enabling way. It is interesting to note how ... Ling Long: Incarnation has a very strong relationship with video games. Both visually and narratively, anime has a very unique principle in being able to link such choices to convey a feeling that we are enjoying daily gambling. The first scene of the anime conveys this idea very well. The characters start in a kind of cave where they need to take resources and go back to their base. As soon as they get what they want, they are attacked by a type of mutant insect that baffles the minds of some, and also by a giant lizard. The characters have a mission, after achieving their objective, they need to escape to survive. This idea is not only in the narrative structure of the anime, but also in the visual, which are very characteristic of shooting games, and in the way the anime is staged. In addition to the expressive use of 3D, which always seeks to travel through spaces, which always leaves the viewer in a great perspective of the action, it also has some frameworks that complement a lot of shooting games. In the action scenes, the characters get to be in first and third person. If Douluo Dalu is an anime that takes advantage of this resource in a very "poetic" way trying to express a more contemplative and enchanting beauty, here the scenarios have a presence that seeks more dynamism in the scenes. The camera at various times even floats through the action. The anime makes great sequences without losing perspective on what is happening in each sequence. Something that is not impossible to do in conventional 2D animation, but that requires much more effort and technique from those who are doing it. It turns out that anime isn't just about that. The plot also explores a certain social and religious context and hierarchy that guides the events of history. One of my “disappointments” was to think that the anime was going to take this idea - of a game narrative - way ahead. It turns out that most of the anime sequences take place only on the floating base of the characters and in some flashbacks. But in no way would I say that such a development of social classes was bad. In fact, anime spends a lot of time contextualizing everything it can from that universe. Even though it was not what I wanted to see, consequently, I ended up being very interested in everything that was presented to me. The direction also managed to express a dramatic possibility of this 3D very well. Not to the point of making you cry, but rather to interest and instigate. If I could make a general summary, I would say that Ling Long: Incarnation tries in every way to play the viewer in the whole context of that universe. It seems to me that there is an almost perfect balance between these ideas.

author: Srodiam
content: Looking at the tags and poster, i thought that this was going to be a cliche serie of monster killing, not entirely different from those series that attempt to ride on Attack on Titan's popularity. To my surprise, Incarnation gives almost no importance to the monsters, instead focusing on the human interactions and struggles in the society that formed on this new world.  After a global earthquake unleashes a myriad of underground monsters on the surface, collective known as Extremozoan, humanity is almost entirely wiped out. The last remains lives aboard the Lighthouse, a flying fortress. In order to maintain the civilization, all interpessoal ... relationships have been abolished. All individuals live only in function to their role on the Lighthouse hierarchy, being divided in 2 segments: Superiors, those who were born with desirable genetic traits, and who are given the most important jobs and best living conditions; and Inferiors, those who were born just as regular people, delegated to the worst living conditions and, "less important" jobs. Only Superiors are given names, while Inferiors are reduced to just to "Worker N° ####".  This is a refreshing change from the usual "medieval magic fantasy" that 95% of Donghua are composed of. Another welcomed change is the animation quality: while most CGI shows have frame drops issues and kinda ugly graphics, Incarnation is really fluid and good looking, some scenes are actually beautiful. This was a really pleasant surprise of a show and i can't recommend it enough.

author: ST63LTH
content: TL;DR: This series is heavily symbolic and shares many plot points with the novel Handmaid's Tale. It is very distressing yet suspenseful it kept me at the edge of my seat beaming on what will happen in the next episode. Ling Long Incarnation is a Chinese donghua set in a post-apocalyptic dystopian, barren world where humanity tries to solve the problem of interplanetary migration but fails due to natural destruction. Extremezoans, a mutated living organism capable of interpersonal communication and coordination dwell in colonies on the ground. It appears that they are scavenger organisms that feed on other living organisms as well as breed fast and ... regenerate faster. Mutants such as the Extremezoans are the main reason why humanity is on the brink of extinction. The Lighthouse is a city in the sky that houses humanity's last hope of survival. The Lighthouse has 3 codes of survival which are rules that can never be crossed: Abolishment of Family, Social Hierarchy and Gene Optimization. Abolishment of Family on the Lighthouse is a rule that forbids intimacy or familial relations. The introduction of this rule lays the foundation that humans must be controlled in order preserve function in the Lighthouse. An example of this are hunters who are bred and trained specifically for combat ability and awareness - Their purpose is the reason they are alive - not to find mating partners - which is heavily enforced by the Light and Shadow Religion on the Lighthouse. Humans on the Lighthouse are segregated into social hierarchy groups called Superior and Inferior. Inferior humans have health defects which deem them unworthy of a high standard of living like Superiors and are often subject to prejudice and maltreatment. Inferiors get pesky jobs like manual labor and they also accompany the Hunters on missions. Some Hunters treat Inferiors as expendable fodder on missions which is a main reason why Inferiors don't have a long life expectancy. When humans on the Lighthouse reach an age where they cannot contribute more than they consume (in food, health expenses etc.) they are sent on a Long Journey on the ground which basically sacrifices them to reduce resource consumption. Gene Optimization on the Lighthouse is a rule that prioritizes Superior human matching. It is pretty much selective breeding where Superior humans with outstanding features like intellect are bred with humans with outstanding physical capabilities. If a Superior child is birthed, both parties will be rewarded heavily by the Lighthouse but if an Inferior child is birthed the child is sent to the slums where the Inferior humans live. It is against this rule for Inferior humans to breed because the worm cakes ration supplied to the Inferior humans is limited. Religion and culture are forbidden on the Lighthouse, there is only one religion that the Lighthouse acknowledges which is the Light and Shadow Religion. This religion is a controlled cult-worship religion that works in strict affiliation with the Lighthouse leaders. It seems the main idea behind this religion was to brainwash and control Superior humans to keep them contributing to the Lighthouse. In one of the earlier scenes, we can see the Chairman of the Light and Shadow Religion (Son of the master of the Lighthouse) praising Superior humans for obeying the codes of survival, one lady was praised for following the gene optimization rule and one man was praised for denying familial relations with his 'father'. All of these aspects work together to form a series of life rules that control and oppress humans on the Lighthouse. This forces everyone to be complacent with the rules and in the chance someone disobeys they are publicly executed to set an example. STORY:  9/10 The story is very descriptive and expansive. Without going into too much detail, we see many perspective and living situations of human life on the Lighthouse. The rules of survival is a genius way that many dystopian survival dramas use to restrict and control the characters and story progression. It also creates the sense of entrapment fearing that the characters will revolt and disobey the rules ultimately facing their demise. Thematically, the story is very aspiring and significant. ART & SOUND: 8/10 The CGI animation isn't as flashy as some high budget series like Mortal's Journey or Perfect World but it is very visually detailed. The characters aren't all that detailed but they have realistic fluidity in their movements. The fight scene between Captain Marc and his trainer is a testament to how fluid their movements are which was a surprise. The angles are also have variation and add suspense in some senses on the ground. Sound design is very good, during the first mission there was a lot of background music and sound effects that added suspense and evoked fear. The scene where the inferiors first encounter the spinal organism is an example of good sound effects and suspenseful music to evoke fear and suspense. CHARACTER

author: GPDonghua
content: General Plot: A disaster and mutant beings feasting on souls has caused humanity to retreat to the "Lighthouse" a floating fortress and final refuge for humaninty. Because of it's limited living space and resources, the "Lighthouse" has become a centrally-planned, ultra-utilitarian, military state. In order to faciliate the most efficient use of resources and preserve the human race, every person is expected to become a cog in the system that runs the "Lighthouse". Familial relationships have been abolished, reproduction is centrally planned, humans are seperated into classes to dictate resource investments, and religion is established to reinforce the caste system and encourage the self-sacrifices needed ... to sustain this society. Despite these restrictions, resources must be gathered periodically from the planet's surface. While the "Lighthouse" has been relatively stable, recent revelations about possible life on the ground and transferrance of leadership (and political ambitions) causes tensions to build and plotting to begin. Once the MC, Marc, gets personally affected, the idealogical battle between self-sacrfices for survival vs freedom erupt. This Season 1 Part 1 is the build up to everything that will happen in this full season. The characters are introduced well, the political climate, living environment and situation are all shown in detail. It is all done beautifully, every aspect of life in the "last bastion of humanity" is clearly shown, from the current living situation, control through relgion, caste system, etc. This season does well in building up the conflict that will very obviously erupt, when someone in power and leadership disrupts the system set in place. The character models and animations are smooth and well done. Even if you don't quite understand the story, the animation quality and action makes this a enjoyable watch. The world building and set up is done extraordinarily well.
